paras: The guest held on the patience, and all of a sudden, the problem was solved. He heard the sound of the Quran being recited. He got up from sleep and observed this wonder that the blind shaikh was reading the Quran by looking at it, and he lost his patience and enquired. “When you are blind, how can you read by looking at each line, and even keep your finger at the word you read. The movement of your finger also indicates that you are keeping it at the exact word.”

He said: “O you, who got rid of the apparent ignorance! You are expressing surprise on the makings of God. I had submitted to God that reading of the Quran is as dear to me as my life and that I have not learnt it by heart; and prayed to Him to grant light to both of my eyes to read it without any interruption. Give the light of sight to my eyes as soon as I lift the Quran to read it. Then, I heard a voice from God: “O man-in-action, who reposed confidence in My support, whenever you needed anything, you have had good speculation about Me, and good hopes, which told you to prosper with every breath of yours. Whenever you wish to read or read the Quran by looking at it, I shall return the sight to your eyes; so that you may read to your full satisfaction. This is according to what the Prophet said in a Qudsi Hadith(s): I do that only which my worshipper thinks that I would do.

“God has since then done like that: whenever I open the Quran to read, that well aware Khabiir who is not unaware of my jobs, that Magnificent King of action, that Singular One, grants me my eyesight like a large lamp which engulfs darkness. That is why a friend of God does not have any hesitation to receive grace, as he returns back to Him its recompense.

If he sets fire to your garden, he provides grapes to you. He gives happiness hidden within sorrow. He provides hand to one who has lost it. He provides pleasureful heart to the ears subjected to sorrowful news. Speaking of “we do not admit which debators usually spell out”, and raising of objections has gone away from us, as is done by the claimants before the judges, when they are sure that they get a great compensation for what has been lost. As I get heat without fire, I am satisfied with it even if the fire is extinguished. When He has given eyesight to blind eyes, such blindness is a bright eye. When He provides light to you without lamp, there is no need to worry if your lamp is put out.”

chapters.title: Total Consonance with God’s Decisions
chapters.subtitle: Attitude of some saints that they are contented with the decision of God, and never pray for their alteration

paras: Now, you may hear the affairs of those guides who do not have any objections to whatever happens in the world. There are saints who seek blessings and reliefs from God, who sometimes join things and separate things and seek alterations of fate. But I know of a few of a different type, who keep their mouths shut from seeking reliefs by supplications. Consonance with fate is their routine affair and they have prohibited upon themselves the seeking of alteration of fate. They take great pleasure in the decision of fate and consider the seeking of relief from troubles as infidelity. Their sense of seeing good in every decision of fate is that they never show slightest and indirect sorrow upon troubles. Whatever that comes to them is considered good. They consider fire as a water of life. Poison becomes sweet in their mouths and the obstructing stones on their paths become gems. Both good and bad are the same for them. How this becoming of good and bad is the same is due to their thinking good of everything. Supplicating for anything is infidelity for them to say: O God! Alter the situation.

chapters.title: When God’s Action Become Man’s Own
chapters.subtitle: Question of H. Bahlul to a Dervish

paras: H. Bahlul asked a dervish of this nature: “How are you?” He said: “How can that person be upon whose decision the affairs of the world proceed. Torrents and streams proceed according to his wish and stars move in the manner which he decides. Life and death are his soldiers, who, as per wish, move about in the streets. He sends sorrows to places, as per his choice; so also joys and prosperity. Those in search of truth follow his steps and those otherwise are helpless in his net. No lips smile in the world without the wish of this ruler and his commands. Not a leaf falls from the tree without his wish and nobody dies without it. No vein palpitates without his wish from the depth of the oceans to the heights of Pleiades.

sections.heading: Speaking for Both Elite and Common Men
paras: H. Bahlul said: What you say is true master: what you say is evident from your face. They are right and there are a hundred times more. But please clarify and speak out in detail in such a way that scholars and the ignorant may understand with their heart and soul and accept them. Please explain it in such a way that the people of normal wisdom should also understand. A perfect speaker is one who keeps all things before the people just as a good host spreads various dishes for his guests on his dining sheet, so that no guest remains without his share; and everyone takes according to his taste. Just like the Quran which has seven layers of meanings which can be taken by the elite and masses as per their requirements.”

The dervish said: “This is believed by all that the entire universe is under the command of God. No leaf from the tree falls without the decision and command of that King on the throne. No morsal of food passes through one’s throat, unless He tells it to pass on. Inclinations and desires of man which are under his control do not act without this command, though he has not seen upon himself. No particle in the earth and the heavens moves, nor a speck of anything moves or flies without following the laws made by Him from the eternity which cannot be explained. And we should also not dare to explain it. Who can count the leaves of all the trees, and when can he bring this as a subject of his discussions. Therefore, hear this much that when all events occur according to God’s command, and when a servant of God holds consonance with them all, he becomes one who desires these events to occur without any formality and desire of reward and approval; rather his nature itself becomes according to them. He will not desire even his life for his own sake, and only as per the command of God. Whatever had been ordained by God from eternity, becomes his law and procedure; and life and death are the same for him. He lives for God and not for wealth; and dies for him, and not out of fear and worries. His faith is for God’s desire and not for the paradise, and the trees and streams therein. He gives up infidelity for His sake and not out of the fear of the punishments of hell. Such a nature comes within him as it is, and not by efforts and struggles. He laughs when he sees the decisions of God; and His commands are like sweet meat for him. When a person is of this habit and nature, tell me, does not the world proceed according to his own decision and command? Then why would he praise God and supplicate to Him, saying: O God, take back this command. His own death and of his children are like sweets in his mouth. For such a faithful man, separation of his sons is like a fruit for a poor old man.

Tell me, why he should supplicate for himself, except where he sees God’s own desire in what he prays for. Such a prayer by him is not a recommendation for others, and relief and mercy upon himself. He is a well guided person. He has blown off the lamp of mercy for himself, at that time when he lit the lamp of God’s love. Love is a hell for his character, and he has completely destroyed love. Every searcher cannot understand the difference in all this, except Daquqi, who did not run for this wealth of knowledge.

chapters.title: Daquqi’s Marvels
chapters.subtitle: Narration of Daquqi and his marvels

paras: Had Daquqi a very pleasing face; he was one in love, and a great man of miracles. He was on earth like the moon in the sky. One moving about in the dark became like those walking about in the moonshine of his light. He would always be on the move and would stay in one place for a little while and not more than two days in a village. He said: If I remain in one home for more than two days, the love of that house will become bright in me. I want to save myself from the honour of long stay in one place. I tell myself, go out and bear the troubles of journeying. I do not want to make the character of my heart to become accustomed to homes; it may not be a special one and different from others.

“During the day he would be on journey and the night in prayer. His eyes were open for the sighting of the Great Lord and sharp sighting like that of the falcon. He was away from the people, not due to bad temperament and not for dislike of men and women. He was very affectionate for the people and profitable to all like water. He was a good intercessionist and his prayers were always answered positively. For both good and bad ones, he was alike in benevolence and well settled: better than a mother and more affectionate than father.

sections.heading: Main Body and Parts: Both Required
paras: The Prophet said: “O leaders, I am like a father for you in affection and benevolence for the reason that you are all parts of my body; and why do you separate a part from the body? “When one separates from main body of group, he becomes useless; and when a part of the body is severed, it dies. So long as that part of the body does not re-join with it, it remains dead, and it becomes unknown as to what happened to its life. If it remains active, it is not a proof of life, as a newly severed part flutters for some time.

And when a part goes away from the main, the main also becomes defective. Its getting separated and re-joining again cannot be explained. This is an imperfect similitude to say that. It has to be understood in the sense that Hazrat Ali is called as a lion. The lion is not like him, nor he is like a lion. This is only a citation to represent bravery.

chapters.title: Greed of Love and Knowledge
chapters.subtitle: Continuation of Daquqi’s narrative.

paras: Go forward from the difference between the example and the exemplified toward the story of Daquqi. Daquqi was as authority on jurisprudence and judgement-giving and was so much advanced in self-discipline and self-control that he had gone ahead of the angels. He had not only outbeaten the moon in the light of worldly matters but had attained such status in the light of the matters of faith that moon would envy. In spite of all self-discipline, ritual remembrances of God and salat, he always used to be in search of God’s specially excellent followers. In all his journeys he used to have this desire to meet such special followers. While starting his journey he used to say: ‘O God, make me a companion of your special worshippers. I consider myself as a slave and carriage for those whom heart recognises. But make me know of such people, my lord, whom I do not recognise myself.’

sections.heading: Greed of More Love and Knowledge
paras: God would tell him: O you advanced fellow, what kind of love is this for me and what kind of thirst is this, that you love me and yet you want to love another? Why do you search for man, when God Himself is with you? He would reply: O my Lord, you are the knower of secrets. You have also opened a path of subservience in my heart. Though, I am sitting upon the ocean, yet I have the greed to collect some water in my pot. I am like David, who had ninety-nine goats, yet he had a greed for one belonging to his companion. His greed was not of the goat but of love itself. Goat is only cited as an approximation of greed. Greed of your love is a matter of pride and status; and the love of any other things is a matter of disgrace and destruction. Passions and greed of men proceed forward, as matters of manliness and pride and the desire of the eunuchs is immoral and disgraceful. Men’s greed is through the front and that of the eunuch is towards the back. The greed of men is an indicator of perfectness of manliness; that of the eunuch is disgrace and deficiency.

sections.heading: Greed for Knowledge Should Not End
paras: But there is a great difference in Daquqi’s love. It has a secret within itself H. Musa ran toward Khizr. Like the one suffering from chronic thirst, which is never quenched by any amount of water, you may also not be at rest at what you have achieved. Go forward and search for more. When you go farther than this, you will see new things which are superior to what you have already achieved. This new thing has no limits. If you have mistakenly considered something as final; give it up for the way to your finality is still to be reached.

chapters.title: Craze for Knowledge Never Ends
chapters.subtitle: Secret of Musa’s seeking of the company of Khizr in spite of the perfectness of prophethood and nearness No end to knowledge

paras: Learn this from H. Musa kaliim (the speaker to God) and get informed as to what he was telling in his enthusiasm. “In spite of possessing that great level of prophethood, I search for Khizr, as I do not have any pride in what I have”. H. Khizr said to Musa: “You have left your community and you are wonderstruck at a new character. You are a king and free of hope and hopelessness, because of your nearness to God. For how long you roam about and up to what extent in the search of things. What you desired is already with you and you are aware of it. You are a sky, and for how long you want to measure the earth.”

Musa said: “Do not condemn me so much. Do not stop the path of the sun and the moon. I shall be going forward until I reach the junction of two seas, so as to become the companion of the Lord, as stated in the Quran: ablugha majma’al Bahraini aw amdia huquba: until I reach the junction of the two seas or until I spend years and years in travel: (Al kahaf: 18: 60). Two seas mean the two kinds of knowledge: apparent (exoteric) and hidden (esoteric). I make Khizr as a means to achieve this object, or I go on forward in search for a long time. I have taken flight for years together with my wings and feathers. What are these few years? Even thousands of years are less. I shall be going on. Yet this going on is not equal to that beloved one. The provision of the beloved’s love is no lesser that love itself. Object of love even when accomplished is not more than love. Love of the beloved is like love. My dear wise man, there is no end to this discussion. Come let us go back to Daquqi.

chapters.title: Journey of the Soul
chapters.subtitle: Return to the left over of Daquqi’s narrative

paras: That Daquqi, may God’s mercy be upon him, said: “I travelled in the east and west for a long time. I travelled for years and months in the love of moon. I was not aware the paths and was fully engrossed in God. I walked bare foot on mud and stones as I was engrossed and wonderstruck. Do not consider these feet to be on the land, as the lover walks, in fact, with his heart. The heart does not know of the path: short or long; and of the destination. Heart does not know all this, because it is engrossed with the beloved. Its marching is of a different type. Short and long are the qualities for bodies, but the walking of the souls is of a different type.

sections.heading: Physical and Spiritual Journeys
paras: Take an example: “You journeyed from the stage of sperm to the stage of wisdom. This journey was completed neither by steps nor by transference. Journey of the soul has no time and space; and our bodies learn to travel from the soul. Everyone cannot see the journey of the soul, but the journey of the body is seen by all. The body has given up the bodily journey, and now proceeds on without qualification in an invisible manner on an unqualified path, as the movement of a lover, who proceeds with his heart and not with the feet.”
He continued to say: “I was one day proceeding enthusiastically, so as to see light (of God) in a man, so that I might see an ocean in a drop, and the sun in a particle.”

chapters.title: Light: Not Visible to Many
chapters.subtitle: Appearance of a similitude of seven lamps on the seashore

paras: And when I walked toward the seashore, the day was reaching its end and it was evening time. I narrate to you what I saw all of a sudden then, so that you may know this secret. I saw seven lamps at a distance, and I went toward the seashore. The flame and light of each of these was reaching up to the sky. I was so surprised that even my surprise got surprised, and the wave of surprise went above the wisdom. How are these lamps so bright, and yet the eyes of the people of the world are not opened by them? The world was searching for these lamps, which are brighter than the moon. There was a strange blindfoldness on the eyes; and this blindfoldness was caused by Him, who guides whomsoever he wants. (He guides whom He wills, Yahdi man yashaa: (Baqara: 2: 142)

chapters.title: Surprises Galore
chapters.subtitle: Seven lamps becoming like one

paras: Then I saw that the seven lamps have become one and its light was tearing off the garments of the sky. Then it broke up and became seven; and my intoxication and surprise all the more increased. Their remaining close to each other was such that which cannot be explained in words. What was seen in a moment cannot be explained in years. Whoever is seen by inner knowledge and consciousness in a moment, cannot not be heard through the ears in years and years of time. As this explanation has no limits, go away from it, as even a little of your appreciation cannot be engulfed by me. I ran fast toward those lamps to know as to out of what these signs of God they are. I became sick, lost my control and consciousness so much that I instantly fell down. For some time, I lay unconscious on the ground. Then I regained consciousness, got up and ran toward the lamps in such high speed as though I was headless and feet less.

chapters.title: Lamps Like Men
chapters.subtitle: Appearance of seven men in the lamps

paras: Instantly the seven lamps appeared as seven men, whose light was reaching the roof of the sky. This light was brighter than the light of the day and was so intense that it put an end to all other lights. I was again taken to surprise upon this wonderful work of nature as to how it happened. I went closer to see more clearly as to what all this is, that is causing giddiness to me.

chapters.title: Abundant Information, Very Few to Note
chapters.subtitle: Seven lamps becoming seven trees

paras: Then each of the men took the shape of trees greenness of which was so pleasing to look at. They were so full of leaves that their trunks and branches were not visible. Extensive fruits were hiding even the leaves. Each tree had sent its branch up to sidrah (Lote-tree); hey; even beyond the sidrah to the region beyond the space. (the Arsh: imperium beyond space from where universe is controlled. Sidrah, as stated in the Quran: Surah: (Alajm: 53: 14, 15, 16): when the Lote-tree was shrouded: iz yaghshaal sidrata maa yaghshaa (behold the Lote tree was shrouded) and near the Lote-tree, beyond which none may pass: Inda sidratul muntahaa.

[Note: Lote-tree under cultivation yields good fruit and shade and is symbolic of heavenly bliss marks the bounds of heavenly knowledge as revealed to men, beyond which neither angels, nor men can pass — Abdulla Yusuf Ali: the holy Quran: pages 1444-5]

The roots of the trees were deep in the earth, which had gone beyond the fish and cow. (Fish and cow considered by the masses of the ancient days upon which the earth was supposed to rest. Even to this day there are people who believe in this:

Renowned scientist, Stephan Hawking starts his very first book “Brief History of time”, published in 1988, refers to an incident in which a well-known scientist (probably Bertrand Russel) gave a public lecture on astronomy describing the orbits of planets around the sun and how the sun, in turn, orbits around the centre of galaxy. An elderly woman said: “What you have told us is entirely rubbish. The world is really a flat plate supported on the back of a giant tortoise.” The scientist gave a superior smile before replying: “What is the tortoise standing on?” the woman replied: “You are very clever, young man, very clever. But it is turtles all the way down.” [page 1, A Brief history of Time, Stephen Hawking, 1989 — Translator].
Their roots were more delightful and fresh than branches and were in such shapes that would upset the minds. When their ripened fruit burst open flashes of light jetted like water.

chapters.title: Knowledge Within Knowledge Within Knowledge
chapters.subtitle: Trees: hidden from the eyes of the people

paras: More than this, was a greater surprise that hundreds of thousands of people were passing that way from forests and fields, craving for shade, spreading rugs for shade and struggling so much for it, but were not at all looking at the shade provided by these trees. Fie upon such unseeing careless eyes. God’s wrath has put a seal upon their eyes that they should not see the moon but only small stars. They should see particles but not at the sun; yet they were not hopeless of the gifts and grants of God. Caravans were passing nearby to these trees, whose ripened fruits were falling down; yet they did not look at. What a wonder is this My Lord! They are collecting rotten apples. They are attacking each other for them. Thirsty people were fighting against each other.

Every leaf and flower on the twigs were telling and continuingly: Ah me! Would that my people knew (what I know): yaa laitata qaumi yalamun: (Yaseen: 36: 26). Announcements were coming from all trees. O unfortunate fellows, come to us. Also, another announcement was coming from other than the trees. We have shut their eyes; they do not have a place to settle as said in the Quran: (kalla la wazar: By no means! No place of safety: (Qiyamah: 75: 11)

sections.heading: People Refuse to Loot at Great Matters
paras: If someone were to tell them to come to this side so as to seek benefits from these trees, they would say: this unfortunate fellow is inebriated and has gone mad as per God’s command. The brain of this fellow has rotten like onion because of his madness of a long time and due to his continuous struggles in his wrongful search of God.

The caller would get surprised and say: ‘O my Lord! What has happened to these fellows? What kind of a curtain of carelessness and misguidance is tied before them? People in spite of their knowledge and wisdom on hundreds of matters, do not ever take one single step toward this. Wise, intelligent and sharp-witted among them are all deniers of this garden and disobedient. Or is it that I myself have gone mad or the devil has struck something upon my head. Every moment, I rub my eyes to feel whether I am seeing a dream or I am seeing imagined scenes. Again, he says: how can it be a dream. I am very much roaming about among the trees, eating their fruits and am in love with them. Then, again, when he looks at the rejectors, are bypassing this garden; and in spite of their extreme need and deficiency they are spoiling themselves for the sake of half-ripe fruits. In their greed and desire for a single leaf from the tree, these helpless fellows are taking long sighs. Going away from these tress and fruits, these people are in hundreds of thousands in number.

sections.heading: Even Prophets God Dejected at Refusals
paras: Then again I tell to myself “I am also a wonderful unconscious fellow! I am just holding an imaginary branch of the tree. I am becoming desperate as said in the Quran about prophets: until, when the apostles give up hope (of their people) and (come to) think that they were treated as liars, there reaches them our help: (hatta, izis taijsa al rusuly wa zannu annahun qad kuzibu jaa’a nasrunaa: (Yusuf: 12: 110). Read this ayat as reading “denial” as something that would reduce the burden, will make you look at yourself as behind the curtain (of protection). The prophets themselves were also put into doubts about their message because of the united denial of the unfortunate deniers. After their becoming victims of doubts, came our support and they were told to ignore the deniers and climb up the tree of the soul and seek benefits of the hidden meanings of all these statements for your own selves. You may yourself enjoy these and also give to those few who have the capacity to receive. This tree of the soul provides to you special and strange knowledge every moment.

The people say: “What is this wonderful call that they are making? Where are forests, trees and fruits? We have been fooled by these mad callers, who tell that there are gardens and fruits here. We have even cleaned our eyes by rubbing them and we do not see any garden. Either it is a wild forest or a rugged path”. The callers tell: “how can such a long affair be meaningless, funny and wrong? We can also say in reply to them: ‘we feel it strange that you do not understand’. Why God has put a seal on them and their thinking, because of which they have become deaf and blind.”

sections.heading: Contradictions Between Muhammad and Abu Lahab
paras: Such were the contradictions upon which even Muhammad was also surprised as to why people reject him. So also, Abu Lahab was surprised at the message of Muhammad. But there is a great difference in the surprise that each one of them had. Let us see what that great king, Daquqi does. O Daquqi, announce loudly and then keep quiet, when those for whom you are saying are deaf.

chapters.title: Herbs and Trees Too Prostrate
chapters.subtitle: Becoming of seven trees as a single tree

paras: Daquqi continued to say: “I went forward very sincerely and found that the seven trees have joined together and become one. Sometimes they were one and sometime later they were seven; and I was observing them in surprise. Then, I saw them in salat all standing in a rank as is done in the formation of congregational prayer. One of them was in the forefront like the Imam and the others standing behind him. The standing, bowing and prostration by the trees appeared very strange to me. Then I recalled the statement of God: And the herbs and the trees both alike prostrate: (wal najmu was sahjaru yasjudan: (Rahman: 55: 6). And also thought, these trees do not have knees and waist and how can they follow the sequence of salat. I got an inner call from God: O the one full of light, do you still have surprises upon our actions.

chapters.title: Trees Become Men
chapters.subtitle: The seven trees becoming seven men

paras: “After a while, the seven trees became seven men in sitting posture of salat before God, and reciting Attahiyat. I was keenly observing by rubbing my eyes to know who these seven great men were and what was their state in the world. I went near them and saluted them in all attention. They replied to my salutation and said: ‘O Daquqi, you are the pride and crown of the honoured men.”

“I thought within myself as to how they came to know of my name, when they have not seen me any time earlier. They realised the feelings of my heart and looked at each other with lowered eyes. They told me: O my dear, why is this still hidden from you. Upon that heart, which is wonderstruck in God, nothing remains hidden from the left and right.”

“I told them: When the truths of all matters are open for the saints, how can they know of formal, apparent names and words. When those great men heard me so saying, they instantly gave me an answer: if Godly men do not recognise one’s name, it is not out of their not knowing, but due to their having gone in the depth of other matters. Then they said: it is our desire, O beautiful one, to follow you.”

“And I said: Alright, but not now; after sometime as I have some problems caused by the alterations of time coming about in the world. So that I may get them solved in the company of the clean people, because in the company of mud grow the grapes.

sections.heading: Impacts of Company
paras: A seed full of capacity to develop with its potentiality joined the company of dead mud in closeness. It mixed up the mud so much that it lost its fragrance and colour; and it ceased to be red or yellow. There at, its limit and extent ceased, and it opened up, spread out and went forward in movements. When it ignored its originality, it lost its face, but various things came out from inside.

sections.heading: Being Within and Out of Time
paras: “They nodded their heads in approval as though they were ready to do whatever I would tell them to do. As soon as they nodded their heads, a great heat and light sprang from out of my heart. With a little time spent in the company of those selected few, I got what all I was hoping for; and found myself to be different from what I was till then. That very instant, my soul became free from the control of time, because time makes a young man old. All changes everywhere, are caused by time. One who gets out of time, gets freedom from the changes brought about by time. O my heart, get out of time for a while, so that you may get rid of the questions of how and why. When you get out of the time for a moment, the question ‘how’ ceases to exist and you become a secret bearer of God, who has no ‘how’; that is, how and what is He alone; that is, without shape and definition. When one goes beyond the questions of ‘how’ and ‘why’, he becomes the secret bearer of God. Time is not aware of timelessness, for the reason that, timelessness involves nothing but extreme astonishment and extreme amazement.

sections.heading: God’s Control on Free Will
paras: “Everyone is tied in his own stable of searching and enquiring. There is a horse trainer in every stable, without whose permission no disobedient horse can get out. If anyone leaves one stable and enters into another, instantly well trained, smart stablemen hold on to its reins and drag it back.”

“Similarly, there are guards appointed for you. If you do not see them, look at the uncontrollability of your free will. When you have free will to do anything of your own, and your hands and feet are free, then why do you remain without doing everything according to your will. This shows that there is some hidden power that controls you. You have resorted to refuse to that invisible guard upon you; and you say that it is due to the fears caused by the warnings or fears of the life.

chapters.title: Daquqi Becomes Imam
chapters.subtitle: Daquqi lead is prayer of the seven men

paras: There is no end to this talk; and therefore proceed, O Daquqi forward, as the time of prayer has come. O the exceptional one, attend to two rak‘ats of salat, so that the world may be beautified by you. O Imam with bright eyes in salat, your bright eyes also should be your Imam. The shariat says that the imamat should not be done by a blind person, even if he has learnt the Quran by heart, is very intelligent and jurist. A man with brightness is better even if he is unlearned. This is for the reason that a blind person cannot protect himself from dirt. Eyes are the basic requirement for protection and piety. The blind man cannot see dirt while passing on the road. Eyes are of such importance. May not God make a mumin blind.

sections.heading: Physical and Internal Blindness of Heart
paras: This is about the blindness of the physical eyes. Internal blindness of the heart is a mine of vices, as it does not have any light in its words and acts. The apparent blind becomes a victim of external dirt; and the internal blind is a victim of inner dirt. The external dirt can be washed away by water from outside, but the inner dirt cannot be washed and goes on increasing. It can be washed by internal water of the tear drops, while weeping on sins when the inner dirts become apparent. When God has called the infidels as dirty people, it does not mean that they are dirty of apparent dirt. This dirt is not on their outside. The appearance of the infidel does not contain apparent dirt, but his dirt is in his faith and manners. The stink of the apparent dirt comes from a short distance of twenty steps, but the stink of inner dirt comes from Rayy to Syria. Rather, his stink goes up to the heavens and irritates the minds of houries and Rizwan. I am telling all this you in accordance with your capacity to understand. I am coming to the end of my life in search of the full understanding. Your understanding is like water and you are like a pot; and when the pot breaks, the water is lost. But this pot has five holes, because of which neither water remains in the pot nor ice. These are your five sense organs — skin, ears, eyes, tongue and nose.

You have heard the command “Keep your eyes low”, but you have not heard it fully. The Quran said: Qul lilmuminin yaghuddu min absaarahim wa yahfazu furujahum. Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze and guard their modesty: (Noor: 24: 30.)

sections.heading: Five Senses and Mouth Betray You
paras: Your mouth also destroys your sense by engaging you in non sensical talk. And your ears absorb all the water of your understanding leaving nothing for the mind to absorb. Similar are the other holes which spill out the water of your understanding. Instead of collecting, your sense organs spill out.

If you take out all the water from a river without compensating by filling water from other sources, it becomes a dry land. This is not the proper time to explain about the conditions of compensations and awards. Those compensations and awards in the rivers come from where when the water is spent out. Hundreds of thousands of animals drink water and clouds also take away the water from it. The river gets its compensation; from where? The guided people know it.

sections.heading: In Praise of Ziaul Huq Husamuddin
paras: Sorry! I have started telling stories in this book, and the object of the explanation of the inner meanings is left out. O, wise Ziaul Haq Husamuddin, the sky and its fundamentals have not brought up a king of wisdom like you. You have strangely come out of the heart and soul, and yet, the heart and soul feel ashamed of touching your feet. I have very much praised the earlier people, but in fact, my intension and praise are for you. You may take anyone’s name for praises and prayers, the praises and prayers themselves find out their own place to say, that it is they only that are addressees. In order to hide the names of the praised ones, God has cited many similitudes and stories. Even though these praises themselves are ashamed, but I feel encouraged, because God accepts the attempts and efforts of the weak ones. God accepts frugals like a piece of bread from a beggar and pardons him; remains satisfied with two drops of tears from the eyes of the blind.

Even birds and fishes understand these hidden meanings. And I have, out of my love for him, spoken in a concise form. This is for the reason that, the remarks of the jealous upon him may be less and they may even not bite their teeth upon his improperly imagined face. The jealous cannot even make proper imagination, just as a parrot cannot sleep in a rat’s pit. Even their imagination of him is an artificial one, which is comparable to the curved hair of the eyebrow and not of the crescent. I shall praise you more times than the five senses and the seven heavens. Now I shall proceed further with Daquqi’s affairs.

chapters.title: Imamat of the Community
chapters.subtitle: Daquqi’s going forward for Imamat of the hidden community

paras: All praises are for God. In salutations to the virtuous, there is a combined praise of all the prophets, in such a manner that the contents of all the cups are put into one trough. This is for the reason that the praised ones, though in large numbers, are none but one. From this angle all religions are none but one. Know this all praises go toward the light of God; but only temporarily toward faces and persons. People do not praise anybody other than the One who deserves praise, but they get misguided due to their improper notions. This is just as moon light falling on a wall, making the wall only as something connected with light.

sections.heading: Mistaking the Unreal for Real
paras: The misguided fellow does not realise this; and when the source of light, that is, the moon sets, the misguided fellow stops praising. Or, when there is a reflection of the moon is in well water, he looks into the well and starts praising the moon. (In the first example, what he sees is only moon light and in the second case, he sees the reflection of moon). His praising of the reflection of moon is actually the praising of the moon itself, even though; out of his ignorance, he is facing toward the reflection and is satisfied with it. Without realising this, if he goes on praising the reflection, ignoring the moon, it amounts to rejection of moon, like infidelity. Out of his unfortunate hard heartedness he has become bold in his misguidance. The moon is above his head but he considers it to be below him.

People are in great confusion with these unreal things which have become their idols. They love false beloveds and when their passions subside, they feel ashamed. They had love for them out of wrong notions and as such, in reality they have fallen far far away from the real world. Your inclination towards your thoughts is like a bush of feathers through which you can enter into the midst of reality. When you lost your feather, you became crippled, and your thoughts vanished. Take care of your feather and do not go after passions, so that the inclination toward the knowledge of reality may take you to heaven. People think that they are enjoying life, and, on this basis, they are plucking their own feathers due to wrong inclinations.

I have become a debtor to the explanation of these points. I am a destitute; give me time to pay my debts. In my waiting for the payment of my debt; I am keeping quiet. I would return to my narration of Daquqi’s affairs, as there is very little left out, as people have stood up for salat.

chapters.title: People Follow Daquqi
chapters.subtitle: The People’s following Daquqi in salat

paras: Daquqi stood in front, and the seven great men followed. They were like a silk fabric and Daquqi was like the decoration on it. This kings followed him in a rank behind this great leader.

The moment takbeer (Allahu Akbar) was said, they became committed to it like the sacrificial animal gets ready to lose life and be ready to leave the world. This is the meaning of takbeer, my dear Imams to say: O God we are sacrificed before You. Just as you say Allahu Akbar at the time of slaughter, you should slaughter yourself and get lost in God. You should say Allahu Akbar and cut off the head of your desires to protect your soul from destruction. Your body should be like Isma’iil who was lain with his face down toward earth, ready to be sacrificed; and your soul should be like Ibrahim who recited takbeer on the dear beautiful son. That is to say: your soul should be dominant, and the body should be dead of passions and the greed. When you say Bismillah in salat, you should be like the slaughtered one. Just as you stand in rank before God on the doom’s day, attending to the accounting of your acts, and in silent supplication to God with tears in the eyes; and later standing like the successful, freed ones.

sections.heading: Questions by God in Qiyaam (as on Doomsday)
paras: God asks: What have you brought for Me out of the time I had given you? In what jobs did you spend your life, and in what affairs did you use the provisions and powers I had given to you? Where did you polish the gems of eyes that I had give to you? Where did you use the five senses, I gave to you: eyes, ears, consciousness are the gems of My abode, the imperium. What did you purchase with them from the earth and how did you spend them? I had given you hands and feet strong like shovels and axes. They were given to you by Me; they did come to you, on their own? Hundreds of thousands of such frightening questions come from the grand court. Such questions come in the standing posture of salat (qiyaam) and the one in salat feels ashamed for some moments; and bends down to hide his face, having no power to stand out of fear and recites the praises of God. Then comes a command from God to rise up and answer the questions. He raises his head and falls down on his face in prostration to hide his face, deficient in actions. Then, again he is commanded to rise and answer, he raises his head and falls down like a swinging snake. Again, he is ordered to rise up and answer; I shall make enquiries with you on the slightest of your actions. He does not have anymore strength to stand up. He feels that a very frightening address has attacked his soul. As a result of this heavy burden, he sits down on his calves and God directs him to say everything in detail: I had given you many things. Tell me, in what manners you expressed your gratitude. I gave money as your capital. What is the profit you have made out of it? As he did not have the capital, nor the profit made of it, he needs someone to intercede for him, to plead for him.

chapters.title: Salutations at the End of Salat
chapters.subtitle: Seeking intercession from the prophets by looking on the right during the doomsday

paras: He turns his face on the right seeking help and support from the souls of the prophets and saints by saluting them. That is to say, he says: ‘O Great men, please intercede in the affairs of this mean fellow, as his feet and coverings are stuck in the swamp. The Prophets say: The day of finding a solution has gone which was there at the earlier stage. You are a rooster which crows at unsuitable time. Go away, you are unfortunate. Pardon us and do not irritate our soul.’

Then he turns his face towards the left side to seek help from relatives and friends, who tell him: ‘You cheat! Make your pleadings with God. We cannot do anything for you. Please pardon us’. When there is no help from this side or that side, his heart breaks into hundred pieces. He gets dejected from all sides in extreme helplessness, lifts both his hands in supplication and says: ‘O God, I am dejected in full; there is none to help me, You alone are the first, last and ultimate. Now is the time to surrender before You alone to grace me and release me from the twisted rope of palm fibre (as stated in Quran: Hablum mim masad: Lahab: 111: 4).’

(O reader!) Do find out these clear signs in salat so that you may know that these events, are certain to occur. O follower in salat, the meaning of obedience is this only that: ‘God alone is the guide, and we are only to receive His guidance. We tell Him: O God! We are obedient to whatever command You give; and even if You punish us, we take it in due obedience.’

Take the signs and direction we have given to you in the performance of salat, and do not do physical standing, bowing and prostration. Do not strike at those acts like a bird that strikes at the grain, and maintain due honour and discipline of salat and bring out the chicken from egg.

chapters.title: At the Time of Difficulties
chapters.subtitle: Daquqi’s hearing of the calls of those in a sinking ship while performing salat

paras: Daquqi started his leadership of the salat on the seashore; the community was behind him. What a grand rank of followers and what a grand Imam. Suddenly, his eyes turned toward the sea, when he heard the sound ‘help, help’ from its side. He saw a ship held up in high tides caught in difficulties, destruction and ill fate. It was a dark night, covered with clouds above and a large waves. There were three darknesses and the fear of sinking. The wind was fierce like Izra’iil the angel of death who had spread out waves on its right and left.

sections.heading: Sighting of Death Causes Terror
paras: The men in the ship were shrunk within themselves out of fear, shouting and making loud sighs. They were beating upon their mouths, and crying. Both the faithful and the infidels were in the same condition showing sincerity in their cries. They were all giving promises and offerings to God in hundreds of humblenesses. All of them had thrown their headgears in sorrow, and in prostration, including those who had not turned toward God in their entire life. They used to tell earlier that their worship and prayers are of no use; and also of hundreds of kinds of means of life without prayer. However, all had lost all hopes from everybody— friends, uncles, fathers and mothers. Both the noble and the sinful had become virtuous, just as even a hard-hearted fellow becomes at the time of taking his last breaths. They did not have any hope of survival either from the right or the left side. When reasonings fail, time of supplications comes.

sections.heading: Repentance at Last Moments
paras: They were all engaged with extreme humility in sighing and praying. The black smoke of their sighs was reaching the sky. Satan was in great anxiety out of his enmity for them and he called out: O worshippers of the dogs, these cries cause two losses to you. They are death and pain. Consider this, O infidels and hypocrites. The ultimate end of all this is the unity of these two troubles. Do you think, if you get relieved, your eyes will be wet with the tears of thankfulness? This will not happen, because of your sensualities. You will not even remember that at the time of danger, God had helped you with His great might. Satan’s voice was coming to them, but ears of the noble ones among them were hearing this.

Correctly has Prophet Muhammad told us, who is the Pole, emperor and the river of clean water: “Whatever the ignorant sees in the end is seen by the wise at the beginning”. Though actions in the beginning have their results unexposed and secret, yet a wiseman sees them; and others see them in the end. Whatever is hidden at the beginning becomes visible for both in the end. O rebellious fellow, if you cannot see the hidden things, why do you follow precautions well before the oncoming of flood?

chapters.title: Meaning of Precautions
chapters.subtitle: Thoughts of a cautious man

paras: Try to understand, what precaution means: keeping a suspicious eye on the affairs of the world and observing oncoming calamities at every moment; in such a way as a man would think when suddenly a lion catches him and drags him in the bushes. Think as to what that man would be thinking while being dragged. This is what one has to think before the occurrence of an event. This thinking is needed, for the master of religious teachings also.

The lion of fate is dragging us toward its den, but our life is engaged in our own jobs and professions. All people have the fear of poverty, as though they are sunk up to their neck in saltish water. If they were to fear the One who causes poverty, the hidden treasures of the world would become visible to them. All of them are sunk actually in sorrow, out of the fear of sorrows. In their search of life, they are caught in the trap of lifelessness.

chapters.title: Prayer for Those in Distress
chapters.subtitle: Prayer and intercession of Daquqi to save those in the ship

paras: When Daquqi saw this doomsday like situation, his feelings of sympathy arose, and his eyes shed tears. He said: “O Lord, do not look at their deeds; spread out your arms and protect them. Bring them to the shore in all safety, as your hands stretch on the land and sea. You are everlastingly generous and merciful. Forgive the sins of their wrong beliefs. You have given hundreds of eyes and ears without taking any price. You have given wisdom and consciousness by taking no bribe. You have given all these to us even before we could have a right and title on them. This is in spite of Your seeing our dishonesties and wrongs. O great one, You alone can pardon us for our great sins and crimes. We have burnt ourselves in the fire of greed and passions. But this supplication to seek relief has been taught to us by You alone. In the honour of the supplication that You have taught us, You have kept lit the lamps of answering them in the darkness of our sins. Hold on to us and guide us. Forgive our wrongs, reward us and release us from the knots of difficulties.”

sections.heading: Supplications of the Beloved of God
paras: As he was making these prayers, he was shedding tears just as a loving mother does with an entirely clean heart for her children. Tears were rolling down from his eyes and the prayers were reaching the heights of the sky. The supplication of those who have lost themselves is a quite a different one, and than the supplication itself and its acceptance are from God. There is nothing between their prayers and the other creatures; and they are such that even their bodies and souls are not aware of them. The true worshippers of God are merciful and graceful. They possess the capacity to set aright wrongs as is the habit of God. They are benevolent and helpful to people without any reward or payment. They are sympathisers and supporters of the suffering lot. Because of their merciful nature they are supporters and intercessors of others in their places of hardship and harsh days. The one in difficulties should search for them, and be careful for this, well before getting into difficulties.

sections.heading: Ungratefulness to Benefactors
paras: As a result of Daquqi’s pray the ship was saved, but the men on the ship thought that it was due to their own efforts that their defending arms have hit the arrows at the appropriate point. Foxes are saved from being caught by hunters with their feet, but the mistaken foxes think that they were saved by their tails. They fall in love with their tails for having protected them from death. In their ignorance of the truth, they kiss their tails and dance in great pleasure. The foolish fox’s ought to protect their feet from the stones, because if they had not had the feet, what could the tail have done?

We are also like the foxes that we think that our feet are great, that they save us from many dangers. Our fragile plans are like the tail which we love madly from right and left. We shake the tail of strategies and arguments so that the hearers may be astonished at our achievements. We desire for the astonishment of the people upon our achievements; and through this we shake the hands of our greed as miracles of godliness, so as to become masters of the hearts of people through this magical attitude. We do not see that we are fallen ones in a pit. O shameless fellow, you are held up in the pit and cave! Do not twirl the moustaches of others to divert their attention towards your achievement. (You being yourself in troubles, you pose yourself as greater than others both physically and spiritually).

sections.heading: First Become Worthy Before Pulling Others
paras: It would be alright, if you hold the people’s hands and pull them towards you, if you are in a good and beautiful garden. First enter into it yourself and then think of benefitting others. You are a prisoner of four elements, (fire, water, air and earth), five senses (hearing, seeing, touching, smelling and tasting) and (six dimensions back-front, right-left, top-bottom), and you have not freed yourself and gone toward spiritualism. What good is it for you to pull others. You are like the owner of a donkey who loves its back side hole. You have found out a wonderful place for kissing and want to take us also with you. when a friend of yours has not agreed to be with you, why do you think of becoming a king? In order to receive the applaud of the people you are putting a loop around your neck (like a buffoon).

O fox, forget this tail of your efforts, dedicate your heart to the people of lively, Godly heart. In the secured place of the lion, there is plenty of meat for you, which the lion collects by capturing its preys. Therefore, do not go after dead animals. O beloved friend! Become one appreciable by God and as a part of the whole. Return to the whole, as a part has to return to the whole.

God says that His sight is fixed on the heart and not on your face and body, as the body is nothing but a mixture of water and mud. You say that you also have a heart. You should know that the heart is settled upon the heights of the imperium, the abode of godhood, and not at the lowly material world. In the blackened slush also, certainly there is water, but you cannot wash yourself and perform ablutions with it, for the reason that, that water in it is under the dominance of mud. Do not call your heart as heart, as the heart is in a high place which is higher than the heavens, and that is the place of the prophets or abdals (saints who have converted the baser human instincts into virtues). Their hearts have cleansed themselves of the mud and flown high and attained elevated status.

sections.heading: Rivers Rush to Oceans, Continents Drag and Slow Them
paras: Leave off the mud and come toward the ocean as it has become an ocean only after giving up the company of mud. Remember that our water is caught in the prison of mud. O ocean of Mercy, take us out of this mud which belongs to the world of Nasoot (material) and absorb us within Yourself (in the world of Lahoot, Your own abode). The ocean tells to the water in the slush: I can pull you toward me, but you boast that you are clear water. Your boasting keeps you deprived. Give up your pride and get into me. The water caught in the slush says I would like to go into the ocean, but the mud catches hold of the water’s feet and drags it toward itself. If water gets its feet freed from the grip of mud, mud will go dry and become strong. What is this dragging of water by the mud? It is the pleasure of pure liquor and accompanying snacks as side dish. In this way are held all pleasures of the world: wealth, grand status and property, gardens, vehicles, swords, shields, kingdoms, houses, children and wealth, each one of these creates anxiety in you. And when you do not get them, you become disturbed. This disturbance upon loss is a proof of the fact that what has been lost had caused semi-intoxication. Do not take more than the need, so that more possessions may not enslave and rule over you. Your arrogance is due to the fact that you think that you have become a master upon your desires; you do not need anybody’s help; and you are entirely devoted to God. This is a claim of loss of interest in materials when you are already imprisoned by materials.

This is similar to water becoming arrogance and telling the mud: I am water. Why should I seek anybody’s help? Just as this water is polluted because of its company with mud, you have confused your polluted heart as a clean heart. That is why, you do not have regard for a man of heart who has no value for materials. Actually, your heart is in love with the milk and honey of the world. Love for milk and honey is a reflection of the taste of the heart, as the pleasure of everything is derived from the pleasure of the heart.

sections.heading: Heart as Substance and World as Accident
paras: [In order to draw a picture or make a writing, some substance like paper or canvas is required upon which to write or draw. The paper or canvas is a substance, and what is drawn or written is accident]. The heart is actually the substance, and the world is an accident. Without heart there is no value to the world. That is; there is no value for the world if the heart does not desire for it. Shadow of the heart cannot become an accident. Heart and its shadow, are both substances. That heart, which is a lover of wealth and popularity, or is dominated by the materials of foul water and mud, or is dominated in the desire to achieve these, as though it is worshipping them, can be a heart only in name. It is not a heart in reality. Heart cannot remain anywhere except in a river of light. Heart is a heart, when its object is God, seeing God only, as otherwise it is just blind. Hundreds of thousands of common and special people do not possess this heart but only one of them; and who is he and where is he? They are the saintly people who have no love for the world. You are only after a part of the heart. Do not go after this part, but go after the entire heart including that part, which should be converted into a mountain by the rest of the heart. Heart is like the ocean which has surrounded the entire land of the world, and scatters gold all over, with its generosity and benevolence. It also spreads the causes of security taking them from God upon all the people of the world with its own authority.

Whoever spreads the flannel before the heart and is ready to receive its grants, receives them. Your flannel is your submission and attendance; but be carefull not to keep in it the stones of sins, so that your flannel is not torn by these stones. Be careful to distinguish between genuine and non-genuine scatterers. You have filled your flannel with stones just as children do, as gold and silver are also stones. As these stones were in reality not gold their contribution to you was only this much, that they tore off your flannel. They have torne the flannel of your truth and increased your sorrow. Children do not identify stones as stones and hold on to them until wisdom comes over. A person is not wise because of his grey hair, but because of wisdom. There is no scope for further arguments in this discussion.

chapters.title: Followers Disagreed
chapters.subtitle: Refusal of the followers in salat to admit the supplication and intercession of Daquqi; and their getting hidden in an invisible curtain; and Daquqi’s astonishment as to whether they were taken over by the wind or gone into the depth of earth

paras: When the ship was saved and reached its destination, the salat of these people also ended. These people started whispering to each other to find out as to who amongst them committed this unwanted act. Everyone talked to each other behind the back of Daquqi in secret. Everyone said that he has not done it by making an inner or outer supplication. One said that this job of supplicating was done by our imam out of sympathy. This is an unnecessary act of a very senseless person. The other said: O friends, I also feel the same. He has become extravagant out of the contraction and limitedness of his heart. He has actually taken objection to act of the Omnipotent God and interfered in His activities.

Then, I looked at them to see as to what these generous great men were talking about. I did not see any of them in the place; all of them had left the place. My keen eyes could not come into grip with them, either on the right or the left; or above or below, as though they were pearls, melted down into water. There were neither the marks of their footsteps, nor was there any dust in the nearabouts to show their walking away. They had all gone into the canopies of God, whose locations could not be seen in any garden. I was astonished as to how the great God has hidden them from our eyes. They are hidden from the eyes in such a manner as the fish dive into the river water and vanish. Daquqi was in distress for years together and cried in their separation for a long time.

You may ask: how can a Godly man care for anybody other than God? How can he think of men along with God? You should know that an ill witted man behaves like an ass in such situations; and you think that they were men and not spirits. Thinking failed in this situation due to the fact that you considered them to be like other ordinary men. You have seen only that which the accursed Iblis said: I am made of fire and Adam is made of clay. He had seen the physical appearance of Adam and not his inner merits. Shut these devilish eyes. For how long and how much do you merely look at the exterior?

O Daquqi, you went in search of the beloved servants of God. You searched for them every day in journeys and prayed to God to take you to such men. You met them on the seashore and lost them. Do not be disheartened, and go ahead still farther with tears in your eyes flowing like streams of water. Do not lose heart; march forward in search of them. Do go in search, because the foundation of any search of materials or other things is starting to search. It results in the expansion of every constriction of the heart. Keep aside all worldly affairs and go on cooing like the cuckoo. Because of the vanishing of those great men, you appear to feel neglected by God. Think over every aspect of the matter and go on praying to God, as God has made His response dependant upon praying as stated in the Quran: Call on Me; I will answer your prayer: Ad‘ooni astajib lakum: (Mumin 40: 60), whosesoever’s heart becomes cleansed of excuses and hesitations, gets his prayers reach the Lord of Majesty and grandeur.

chapters.title: Cow as Gift of God
chapters.subtitle: Return to the story of the seeker of halal food without efforts during the days of David (AS)

paras: The story of that poor man came to my mind who was craving before God, day and night seeking halal food without putting efforts, struggles and hard work. Earlier, I have spoken of some of his affairs which could not be continued as there came about other discussions. His affairs cannot remain untold as, with God’s grace there are many points of wisdom in them.

The owner of the cow saw him and angrily told him: “My cow has fallen into your cruelty. Tell me why you killed my cow. You are a foolish thief”. The poor man replied: “I have been seeking food from God by presenting myself with sighs and cries before Him. For years together, I was engaged in this alone and finally God sent a cow for me. By looking at it I got up thinking that my food has reached me. This was the result of long sought-after supplication which was answered in the form of the cow which I slaughtered”.

chapters.title: Raising of Dispute
chapters.subtitle: Going of both Parties to David (AS)

paras: The owner of the cow got angry at this reply; caught hold of the poor man by his collar and gave many blows on his face and dragged him before prophet David saying: “come, your foolish, cruel fellow! Stop those unconvincing arguments, O mischievous fellow. Come to your senses and be wise. What kind of prayer is this? Make no fun of me, of my life, my face and of my beard, you fearless fellow”.

sections.heading: Confidence in Supplication
paras: The poor man said: “I have supplicated to God many a times and in doing so I have swallowed my own blood. I know with certainty that the prayers are always answered in approval. You may not believe in this. In such a case, you should dash your head on a boulder”.

The cow-owner started addressing the people saying: “O Muslims, come and see the arrogance in this senseless talk. How long do you speaker of non-sense speak like this. Bring forth an evidence to say as to what kind of supplications of is. Tell me O Muslims, how can his prayer transfer my materials to him? If this were to be the way, the entire world would have forcibly taken over the materials of others with prayers. If this were to be so, blind beggars would have become honourable and rich. Day and night, they would engage in prayers and praises to God saying foolishly: ‘O God, pray give us’. They also say: “So long as You do not give, certainly no one would give us. O Opener of the knot, open this knot. The profession of the blind is always flattery and prayer, yet they do not get anything more than a piece of bread.”

People said to the poor man: “What this man says is true; and this seller of the prayers is wrong. How can a supplication make one an owner of property? How can the law put its seal on it? Sale, grant, will or gift and some similar deeds can make you an owner of a thing. In which book of law, it is written that you make a prayer and become owner of a thing. Either give back his cow to him or go to jail. Get into the jail or return his cow to him and do not speak nonsense.”

The poor man turned his face toward the sky and said: “O Honourable God of generous and merciful nature! I had prayed to You with this desire; and what I did with You was not seen by anybody. You only put the supplication in my heart and raised a hundred hopes. I had not supplicated on my own. Like Yusuf, I had also seen in a dream.

sections.heading: Yousuf’s Dream Gave Vigour
paras: Yusuf had seen the sun and the stars falling in prostration before him like servants. He had relied upon this true dream. He did not opt for the well and the prison on his own. He had his reliance only upon his dream and the oncoming slavery and the disgrace to lesser or larger extent before the people. His confidence in the coming true of the dream was so much. He had so much confidence upon his dream as he had on the bright lamp before him. When he was felled into the well, a sound fell into his ear from God: O young brave man, one day you will be a king; so much you will repulse back their cruelty on their faces. The announcer of the sound could not be seen, but the heart recognised the announcer with His impact. The Quran says: wa awhaina ilaihi litunabbi annahum bi amrihim haaza wa hum laa yash ‘uruun: (we inspired to him: You will tell them of the deeds of theirs when they know you not: (Yusuf: 12: 15). This sound provided to Yusuf courage, strength and relief and gave a new vigour to his soul. With this majestic sound, the well became a garden and honourable place just as fire had become a garden for Ibrahim. After this, whatever difficulties he faced, became pleasurable, because of the new vigour he had received.

sections.heading: One Who Sees the Dream of “Alastu”
paras: This is just as the sound of “Alastu” given to the faithful, which gave them a taste of vigour till the doomsday. God had asked all the humans: Alastu birabbikum: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes verity: Qaalu Balaa. (we do testify): Shahidnaa: An taqulu yowma alqiamati inna kunna an haaza ghafilin. Lest you should say on the day of resurrection: Lo! Of them. We were unaware (Kahaf: 7: 172)

This is, so as to see that they should not have any grievance when they are put on trial; or they should not have any difficulty in accepting God’s commands, to do and not to do any act. Bitter morsal becomes sugar for them, and the thorns become sweet smelling plants and stones become gems. Commands of God, hard to obey and bitter in taste become sweet in taste and easy to obey.

One who has no belief in the promise of Alastu; (Am I not Your Lord) will not have the taste of sweetness, and as such, he refuses to swallow, and spills out. One who has seen the dream of Alastu remains fully engaged in full pleasure in the obedience of commands. He carries this great burden of obedience, like the intoxicated camel without any slackness, pain and doubt. The camel releases the froth of its saliva from its lips to prove the heaviness of the weight and to prove that it feels no pain of the burden. It becomes like a male lion in vigour, and it also reduces the intake of food due to this burden. This is like its going hungry for a number of times in its desire for the she camel. Hills appear like hair to it.

sections.heading: Nearing of Alam Nashrah: (Expanded Your Heart)
paras: One who has not seen the dream of Alastu cannot remain as an obedient servant and fully inclined disciple. Even if he becomes a disciple, he will have a hundred hesitations in his heart. If he is thankful for a moment, he raises grievances for one year. He keeps one foot forward in the path of religion and keeps another backward. This, he does due to lack of full confidence. I have the burden of debt upon you to explain the meanings of what I said in this regard. I keep a chess piece before you for this as the explanation of this has no end. You may hear Alam Nashrah laka sadraka: Have we not expanded you your breast: (Inshirah 96: 1) to understand these points.

Alam Nashrah made easy all difficulties in the life of the noble Prophet. If God expands your breast also, things will become easy for you. The noble Prophet recalled the statement he had made at the time of God’s questioning as referred to “Alastu” that God is with him. And when a person reposes full confidence in God’s being with him, he will have the courage to do anything and happily bear with any trouble that comes.

As the details of this matter have no end in explanation and they have to be understood by one’s own efforts and God’s grace, let me delay for some time and drive my donkey toward the owner of the cow for the present.

The poor man said: “This treacherous man has called me blind taking me as a criminal. What he said is similar to what Iblis said about Adam. He had seen Adam’s exterior and not his inner greatness. So also, this man calls me as a blind beggar before the people, while, in fact, I am a beggar before God.

I have not prayed to God not as an unseeing blind fellow. I have confidence in Him and begged before Him alone. Blind beggar expects from the people, but I have not done so: I begged before God for everything, and this makes all difficulties bearable. This fellow has not seen my sincerity and devotion to God. My blindness is a blindness of Love. You do not know that love makes one both blind and deaf. I am blind for everything other than God and see God in full, and this alone is the demand of true love. O God, do not keep me along with other blind; You are the central point of graces, around which I am orbiting.

Just as You had shown a dream to the truthful Yusuf, which became his inspiration and support, your benevolence has shown me a dream which was due to my innumerable supplications. People do not understand my secrets and call my sayings as non-sense. I do not blame them as they do not know of the hidden secrets. None can know this except You the Knower (‘Allaamu) and the protector of secrets (sattar).

His opponent, the owner of the cow said: “Tell the truth, O uncultured fellow, why do you turn your face toward the sky. You commit treacheries and put the people on wrong side and talk of your love and the nearness with God. With what face do you talk of all this? You have a dead heart, and you turn toward the sky.”

The entire city came to know of this quarrel and that poor muslim fell in prostration on the ground and said: “O God, do not disgrace this poor slave. Do not let my secret be known, even if I am wrong. You know fully well that for nights together I have been calling You in full devotion. People may not understand this, and may not value it, but before You all this is clear like a bright lamp. They are asking me to give back the cow, which You sent for me. You know, I have committed no wrong.

chapters.title: Court-Trail Begins
chapters.subtitle: H. Dawood’s coming out and hearing of both the parties and questioning the poor accused and his replies

paras: H. Dawood came out and sought for the details. The complainant said: “O prophet of God, do hear my case. My cow entered into the house of this man and he slaughtered it. Please ask him why he did so.”

H. Dawood asked him: O good man, tell me why you destroyed the property of this noble man. Be careful, do not talk nonsense. Bring forth your reasons, so that this complaint and claim may come together to make it easy to decide”.

The accused poor man said: “O Dawood, for seven years day and night I prayed to God and asked Him to provide halal provisions without efforts and work. Men and women are aware of my prayers and even children talk about it. You may ask anybody about this matter so that he may speak of the truth without fear and compulsion. You may ask the people in the open or in privacy as to what this poor man in torne clothes has been saying. As a result of these prayers and cravings all of a sudden, I found a cow in my house. My eyes instantly got blind, out of the pleasure of the acceptance of my prayer by God not for the pleasure of eating its flesh, and I slaughtered it in this happiness; and as a matter of thanks to God, and not to eats its flesh, but to distribute it among the poor”.

chapters.title: Cultivator Entitled for Harvest
chapters.subtitle: H. Dawood’s judgement against the cow slaughterer

paras: H. Dawood said: “Wash out all these things from your heart and present legally supporting averments. Do you consider it right that I should establish a wrong precedent under the law? Who had granted this cow to you or who had sold it to you? Without these means, you cannot become its owner. How can you harvest a crop when you have not cultivated it? My dear uncle, consider the earning of a thing as cultivation of land. So long as you do not cultivate, you cannot reap the harvest. You are the owner of whatever you sow and harvest, as otherwise this falls as a cruelty upon you. Go back, return the property of the muslim and do not make baseless arguments. Go away, borrow from others, and give its price to the owner. Do not make untenable submissions”. The poor man said: “O king, you are also telling the same which these cruel people are telling”.

chapters.title: Seclusion Provides Inner Knowledge
chapters.subtitle: Craving of the poor man before God upon the judgment of H. Dawood

paras: The poor man took a long sigh and said: “O God of every place where there is an odd and even number”. He falls in prostration before God and said: “You are the Knower of every injury, put that light into the heart of Dawood”, so saying, he started crying and wailing so much that Dawood’s heart started going away from its place.

Dawood said to the claimant of the cow to wait and give him time to think over, and not to hurry, so that he may go over in seclusion to perform salat and seek guidance from God, the knower of secrets.

He also said: “I have that habit in the salat which reciprocates with me in all that I say, as I know the meaning of qurratu ‘aini fii alsalat (the coolness of my eyes is in salat: as stated by the noble Prophet: Hadith(s)).

sections.heading: God’s Special Grants to Man
paras: “As a result of the cleanliness of my heart I have an opening in it through which the message of God comes directly without any intermediary. Messages, rains of the graces of God, and His lights originate from my mine and enter into my house through this opening. That house is a hell which does not have such opening. The fundamental job of faith and religion, O servant of God, is to create such an opening. Do not strike your axe on all bushes to make way but strike it to make such opening in the heart. You do not know that the light of the sun is only a reflection of the real light of God that is falling on the sun from behind a curtain. You consider this light visible to the eyes which even the animals see. But you do not know of the great honour that God has granted to man, which God has called as karramna (we have honoured as stated in the Quran: we have honoured the sons of Adam; provided them with transport on land and see (wa laqad karramna bani Adama wa hamal naahum fii al barri wa albahr.. (Bani Isra-il 17: 70)

sections.heading: Prophets Seek Seclusion to Teach the People
paras: I am sunk in His light like the sun is and I do not see any difference between myself and His light. My going in seclusion for the performance of salat is only with the purpose of teaching the people, as personally, I do not need it. This is a wrong step by me to go away from the people but is a right step for the teaching of the common folk. This is actually a trick like the one played in the battlefield, as otherwise people will not follow the visible method.

There is no provision for the speaking of the secrets of all this, as otherwise I would let flow a river of secrets. In this manner, H. Dawood was speaking out, with which the wisdom of the common people would be set on fire; he was pulled back from behind by an invisible hand and prevented from revealing secrets, which said: Stop! Do not go further. I have no doubts on what you say, about God’s being one with all.

chapters.title: Further Trail of the Case
chapters.subtitle: H. Dawood’s going into seclusion to seek the truth of the matter

paras: H. Dawood prevented himself from further talk, maintained full silence and went into seclusion; closed the door and sat the niche for a supplication to be answered. God revealed to him, what all had to be revealed; and he became aware of the punishment for revenge. He saw such things which no one has seen, and also hidden those secrets which increased his anxieties.

The next day, the parties to the dispute came and stood before H. Dawood. As was on the previous day, the proceedings went on and the complainant immediately started his abusive language telling: “O useless fellow, give back my cow and feel ashamed of your acts before God, that such an event has occurred in the days of the Messenger of God, which is entirely unjust and unsuitable. After slaughtering my cow and eating its flesh without any fear, this unworthy fellow has resorted to treacheries saying: he has been praying to God for so many years and asked for it and God gave it to him. O prophet of God, can this be legal? Cow was my property, and how could God give it to him?

chapters.title: Claiment Advised to Wave Off
chapters.subtitle: H. Dawood’s order to the cow’s owner to forget about the cow; and the cow owner’s condemning H. Dawood

paras: H. Dawood told him to keep quiet and waive off the claim of the cow upon this muslim. “When God has put a curtain upon your acts, it is required that you should keep quiet and understand the duties of hiding the acts of others”. But he said: “Oh, what kind of justice is this? Are you going to make a new law for me? Your justice is so well known, as if, the earth and sky are all fragrant with it. But what you are doing is such that, it cannot be done even with blind dogs. It is such that with it even rocks and mountains will shatter into pieces”. In this manner, he went on lamenting and shouting: this time to be a time of great cruelty; and pleading to the prophethood of H. Dawood, not to do this type of cruelty to him.”

chapters.title: People Support Oppressors
chapters.subtitle: H. Dawood’s command to him to give all his possessions to the poor man

paras: Thereafter, H. Dawood told him: “O mischievous fellow, give all your property to him; as otherwise, your affair will be very difficult. I warn you, so that your cruelties may not be exposed.”

The cow owner tore down his clothes and started putting dust on his head as was the practice of protesters and lamenters telling: “every moment, you are adding to the cruelties upon me.” Then, he continued to abuse him.

H. Dawood called the complainant closer to him and said: As you are not fortunate enough to keep your secrets remain as secrets, O impatient fellow, your cruelties are getting exposed moment by moment. Now you have taken the court and its proceedings like garbage the street. How unfortunate for an ass like you.”

All the blabberings of that fellow made H. Dawood angry and he warned him not to destroy himself. Go away from here! Your wife and children shall also become the property of that poor man as slaves. Hearing this that man started beating his chest with both hands and went on running helter skelter, in all foolishness.

sections.heading: Oppressor and the Oppressed
paras: Looking at this the crowd also started blaming H. Dawood, as they were not aware of that fellow’s hidden acts. How can that fellow find the difference between the oppressor and the oppressed, who is unworthy like a piece of straw flying in the air.
