Only he finds the difference between the oppressor and the oppressed, who has cut off the head of his own oppressions. Otherwise, every oppressor, who has the arrogant ego alive within himself, becomes an enemy of the oppressed, as the arrogant ego is always cruel, not only upon others, but also upon its possessor. Everyone obedient to his ego goes mad in the oppression of others. The dog always attacks a poor man and bites him to the extent possible. Dignity and grace are found only in the lions and not in dogs, as lions do not snatch the prey caught by their neighbours.

The common people who are always against the oppressed and admirers of the oppressors, came out of their hidden meanness and started abusing H. Dawood. They turned towards him and said: “You are a selected prophet of God. You ought to be benevolent to us. This does not suit you to show this open cruelty to the cow-owner. You have been cruel to an innocent person for no reason.”

chapters.title: Cow-Owner Was a Murderer
chapters.subtitle: H. Dawood’s decision to take the people to the (forest) to expose the secrets

paras: H. Dawood said: “Friends, the time has come now to expose his hidden secrets. Get up all of you, so that we may all go towards the forest. Men and women, come out of your homes so as to know the hidden secret. In the forest there is a strong well-developed tree. Its branches are well spread and thick, so close together as though they form a tent standing upon the pole of the tree trunk. I smell of blood from its roots. There has occurred a murder in its roots and that is of the master of this accursed fellow. This criminal has killed him and looted the wealth of his master. O free people, know this, that he was his slave.

This young man is the grandson of that master. He was a child then and therefore unaware of all that happened. Till now, God’s indulgence had kept it a secret; but for his thanklessness, this is exposed now; that he never took care of the children of his master, not even on the days of feasts. He has not given a morsel of food to the destitutes. He has not remembered the rights that others have upon him. So much so, now, for the sake of a petty cow he has thrashed grandson of his master on the ground. He has himself lifted the curtain from his sins, as otherwise God had kept his crimes hidden.

In these days of trials, the rejectors and sinners themselves tear up their curtains. Oppressions remain hidden among the secrets of life, but the oppressor himself keeps them before the people, telling them: “look at these oppressions committed by me that have raised their horns and see clearly the cows of the hell.”

chapters.title: Sins Are Themselves Evidences
chapters.subtitle: Hands, feet and tongue stand as witnesses against oppressors

paras: Your hands and feet stand as witnesses against you in this world itself to speak of your inner feelings. Your conscience itself acts as your own attorney and tells you to spell out what you do and believe. Particularly at the time you are in anger and revengeful and in flamboyant talk, it reveals even the minor details of your acts. Your cruelties and excesses themselves become your attorneys and tell the hand and feet to expose them. Your wisdom itself acts as a witness against you, particularly when you are enthusiastic, angry, and revengeful. The authority of God has appointed your conscience as your attorney so as to establish your offences even when you are alone and forlorn in the forests. Such witnesses can be brought before you even on the day of resurrection to reveal your secrets.

sections.heading: Man’s Conscience, a Witness Against Him
paras: “O the one whose two hands bring about cruelties and mischiefs, do not require some outer witnesses. They are there within yourself, who stand against you. There is no need to be well known for your harmful nature as your fiery inside becomes clear to everybody. Your inner quality brings forth a hundred sparks every moment telling the people: look at me! I am the one belonging to the hell. I am a part of fire and I am returning to my whole. I am fire and not light so as to be able to go toward God.”

In this manner this cruel denier of the rights of others has played so many tricks for the sake of a cow. He has taken away a hundred cows and camels belonging to this poor man. This is the inner disqualification, which does all this; and therefore, run away from it. He never showed humility before God on any day and said “O my lord” in a painful voice to say that the One before him may be happy. And also saying: if I have any harm to him, convert this harm into gain. If I have killed anybody by mistake, his relatives are entitled for compensation. Upon the commitment of my telling: ‘yes, you are my lord’, when You had asked me ‘whether You are not my Lord’, my life may be taken as entitled to compensation. Repentance and seeking pardon make a pebble, a pearl, and evil acts become good. You, as a free thinker, may think about the justice that conscience does.

chapters.title: Reasoning of Judgement
chapters.subtitle: People go toward the tree

paras: When all the people went towards that tree, H. Dawood ordered for his hands to be tied behind, so as to expose his sin and crime, so that the flag of justice may be hoisted in the forest. He said: “O cur! You have killed this man’s grandfather. You were a slave but by killing him you became a master. You killed your master and misappropriated his belongings. But God has revealed all this: your wife was your master’s maid; and she has also committed offence against her master. Everyone she gave birth to, male or female, belong to the heirs of the master. You are a slave, and all your earnings also belong to them. You wanted a judgement as per law; and this is that judgement. You have killed your master with great cruelties. He pleaded to you here to leave him alone and give peace. In your hurry you buried the knife are that appeared very frightening to you. The head of the murdered master and the knife is buried here. Open up the ground, you will see a knife with this cruel dog’s name inscribed on it. He has done such cruelties to his master. The people dug up the ground and found the knife and his master’s skull. People started shouting loudly; and everybody cut off his zunnar (sacred thread of the zoroashtrians) from the waist. Everybody started seeking H. Dawood’s pardon as they had been spoiled due to suspicions upon his judgement.

chapters.title: People Are Curious About Crimes
chapters.subtitle: H. Dawood’s order to avenge the murder after setting up evidence of crime Miracles of H. Dawood

paras: Then, H. Dawood called upon the poor man who had slaughtered the cow to avenge the killing of his grandfather. He ordered him to avenge with the same weapon. How could his treachery remain hidden from God? Though God’s indulgence is very sympathetic, but it disgraces when the mischief goes beyond limits.

sections.heading: Murders Cause Curiosities
paras: Murder does not remain hidden for long. It creates curiosity in every heart to find out the cause and solve the difficulty. The demand of the justice of the Lord raises its head about the murder and the cause of murder in every heart, raising questions as to what happened, how it happened and why it happened, just as the seeds sown in the garden raise their heads. Murders cause many curiosities in the hearts of the people resulting in itches in the hearts, causing discussions and seeking of results.

When the secret of the acts of H. Dawood became well known, it was taken as his miracle. People came over to him without their head gears and kept their foreheads on the ground before him saying: “we were all blind and refused to consider what all you said. But we are helpless, as we have no eyes to see. We have already seen many wonders in you. it is well known that stones talked to you when you had asked Saul (Talut) to take you to the battlefield. You had taken three stones and the sling and killed hundreds of thousands of enemies. Your three stones had converted into hundreds of thousands of pieces and each one became each one’s killer.

Iron in your hands became soft like wax, when you had learnt to make the coat of mail. Hills sing along with you and recite Pslams like expert reciters. Hundreds of thousands of eyes of the heart opened at your signs and got informed of hidden matters. Above all these is the vigour given by you and the life granted by you that last for ever. This is the life of all other miracles, which gives eternal life to a dead man. When a cruel man is killed, the entire world gets a life; and everyone again becomes a good servant of God.

chapters.title: Hidden Conclusions and Lessons
chapters.subtitle: To explain that man’s inner self is like the murderer who claimed the slaughtered cow; the slaughterer of the cow is like wisdom; and H. Dawood or a teacher are vicegerents of God, who with God’s granted power and support, killed a cruel man; and that one can become rich without making efforts and earnings Jesus Christ’s running away from fools to the hilltop; another man following and questioning him

sections.heading: Intricate Lessons of the Story
paras: Kill your Nafs: (inner mischievous self) and give life to the world. It has killed its master. Enslave your Nafs. Be careful to note that the claimant of the cow is also like your inner mischievous self, who has made himself a master and leader. The entire lot of people got relieved when he was killed, and this amounts to the killing of your mischievous inner self, which upon getting killed makes you pure.

The killer of the cow is like your wisdom and do not reject it just because it killed the cow. Wisdom is a prisoner of the inner mischievous self and it desires that God should grant it all provisions without putting efforts and hard work. The receipt of provisions without efforts is dependent upon the cow, killing which was necessary as it was the root of all mischiefs. However, it was by killing the root of all mischiefs ultimately resulted in the receipt of provisions without efforts and work, though it came after a long time. Nafs (inner mischief) says as to why you killed the cow. It considers the cow as its physical form. Wisdom which was in the form of the supplicator for free provision had become a pauper due to the killing of his grandfather; and his murderer, the Nafs, had become the owner of all his wealth. Thus, there was a tussle between the mischievous inner self of the cow owner and the wisdom of cow killer.

sections.heading: How Provisions Received Without Efforts
paras: But do you know as to what is this acquiring of provisions without physical efforts. Those are the provisions, of the spirits, which are provided by the prophets. But it is dependent upon the killing of the Nafs (represented by the cow) which ultimately led to wealth for which no efforts were put.I would have explained to you everything about the receipt of provisions without efforts. But I cannot, because I have eaten something yesterday which has made me semi unconscious. I would have provided to you all the basics upon which you could proceed. Yet, my hesitation to say all is due to my having eaten something, is just a statement for argument’s sake, because that everything that comes to everybody, is from the unseen sources only. Yet, I tell you, as to why I relied upon the spoken arguments. This is because, I have learnt this method from those with miraculous glances like the prophets.

sections.heading: Reasons upon Reasons; Grounds upon Grounds
paras: You should know that there are reasons upon reasons, but you should not simply look at these worldly (rational) reasons; and look beyond. Prophets have come to cut off these rational reasons. They have established the miracles upon saturn. H. Musa split the ocean without any visible means. He got heaps of food in the form of mann and salwa, without any means to obtain. For the sake of H. Ibrahim, sand had converted into wheat flour and rough wool had become soft silk for Musa’s mother. The entire Quran speaks of the cutting off of the material, rational reasons and material (intelligential) grounds giving the example of the honour and victory of person with no means like H. Muhammad; and killing of Abu Lahab who possessed everything.

Birds dropped two-three pebbles upon the elephants of the Abbyssinian army of Abraha and defeated him. The pebbles dropped by the small flying birds on the huge elephants pierced their bodies and killed them. H. Musa hit, with the flesh of a cow upon a murdered person on his shroud to make him alive so as to enable him to stand to give the names of his killers to avenge them. In this manner, the Quran from the beginning to end refers to the absence of apparent reasons and grounds for occurrence of events. These matters cannot be understood by wisdom; you should meditate for long to understand them.

sections.heading: Apparent Wisdom and Inner Sight
paras: Philosophers are held up within the bounds of rational arguments, but those who ride upon the horse of wisdom in entirely (not partial alone), go beyond common wisdom toward something more. The wisdom of your wisdom is the essence; and your wisdom is just its rind. Stomachs of animals go in search of the rinds of fruits. But those who search for the pulp and essence discard the rind, considering pulp and essence as worthy for them. When the rind of wisdom produces hundreds of arguments, it is not possible for the entirety of the essence of wisdom to proceed, without submitting itself to yaqeen (certainty of sight)?

Wisdom makes black sheets after sheets of white paper with its arguments; but the wisdom of wisdom fills the surroundings of the world with its bright moon. Wisdom of wisdom or perfect wisdom is not dependent upon black ink and white paper; but its bright moon rises on the hearts and souls of the people. The value of a purse is due to its contents of money and gold; and it has no value without money and gold in it. Just as the value of the body is due to the soul, the value of the soul is due to the light shed by the brightness of the lovely moon. If the white paper and black ink get their value by the words they contain, which are due the light shed by the night of power (“lailat ulqadr”: Qadr: 97: 1) which is a night better than a thousand months. Similarly, the worth of the body is due to the reflection of the beloved God. If the soul is without receiving the reflection of the brightness of the beloved God, He would not have called the rejectors as dead bodies.

sections.heading: Difficulty in Realising Reality
paras: Though the power of my talks is digging up a stream, but water will come into it after a long period. That is to say: what I say cannot be understood now, but only in the days to come (in future). Though in every period there have been those to explain but they proceeded further on what their earlier one’s had said. Is it not a fact that, Torah, Zabur and Injil stand as proof of the truthfulness of the Quran. Demand unlimited provisions without hard work and efforts, so that Jibra’iil may bring apples for you from paradise. Rather provisions will come to you from the Lord of paradise without undergoing the trouble of farming over the farmer and the farmland. Because the profit and essence of the bread comes from the bread given by Him without the admixture of the husk and a go-between. The taste of bread is hidden in the observable features of the bread, which is kept on the dining sheet; and the bread of saints is without these features and the dining sheet.

sections.heading: Difference Between Justice and Equality
paras: Food of the soul does not come about without a just and equitable master like Dawood, who did not do the justice as per law but by equity byepassing the law as happened in the case of the cow slaughter. The owner of the cow demanded justice as per the law to direct the cow-killer to return his cow. But Dawood went beyond justice and showed equity (Adl) to meet the ends of justice by taking away from us as per the materials that actually belonged to the cow-killer. When (Nafs—mischievous inner self) sees you moving along with your master, it becomes obedient to you, just as the owner of the cow yielded to the command, when Dawood’s breaths informed him of the truth. Wisdom dominates upon the dog of your Nafs in your efforts to achieve things when it sees you in the company of the shaikh as happened when the cow-owner saw the cow killer with H. Dawood. Nafs is a python with hundreds of treacheries and designs but the face of the shaikh, acts like emerald which makes it blind (as is commonly believed). If you want to defeat the mischievous cow-owner, drag him, like a donkey to the shaikh.

sections.heading: People’s Weakness Exploited by Cheats
paras: Mischiefs of the Nafs and body were not understood by the common people. They, as well as the Nafs cannot be overcome without the inspiration from God, as happened when H. Dawood came in in-between. Everyone, similar the Nafs became a friend of the cow owner, but not H. Dawood as he was a master. Only he is a master who has changed himself so much that he ceased to be in his physical body of worldly demands, who as a result of his efforts was made by God as soul and heart in entirety.

sections.heading: People’s Weakness Exploited by Cheats
paras: People in general are like sick men and naturally each of the sick man is helpful to the other sick man. They have spiritual sickness also and therefore, go to the help of cruel fellows. There are plenty of tricksters and mean fellows who claim themselves of spiritual attainments like H. Dawood had, and the uncultured go close to them and clap at them. They are like the foolish birds who upon hearing the mimicked sound of the voice by the hunter, get cheated and fly toward him and get caught in his trap. Be careful about those misguided fellows, who cannot differentiate between the original and counterfeits and run away from them even if they talk of apparently meaningful words. They consider the free man and their victim on the same footing. Their claim of perfectness is doubtful. There may yet be many intelligent men, but their intelligence is only verbal without the capacity to realise the difference between real and imitation. Such fellow are fools deserving to be kept away. Run away from them just as the deer runs away from the lion. Do not go near them, if you are wise and bold.

sections.heading: Treacheries of the Nafs
paras: If you want to protect yourself from the python, do not ever remain away from the master. Become humble like dust before the shaikh, who knows the secrets of matters so as to make your dust effective and purify it like alchemy. Your Nafs has a hundred tongues to speak, and each of these tongues has hundreds of arguments. Its treacheries and designs are such that they cannot be explained. But when it faces a friend of God, its hundred-yard-long tongue becomes short and dumb. The Nafs of the claimant of the cow had a long tongue which produced hundreds of treacherous arguments, with which all the people of the city were misled; but not the truth knowing Dawood. The Nafs keeps the Quran and the rosary in its hands, but dagger and sword in its sleeves. Do not get cheated by its treacheries which are based upon the misinterpretations of the Quran itself, and do not become its secret- bearer and partner. It will take you toward a pond for performing ablutions, and while you’re doing so, it will forcefully push you in its depth.

sections.heading: Even Wisdom Gets Cheated
paras: Wisdom is a noble light and the best of searchers, yet it gets dominated by the lures of the dark Nafs. This is because, your Nafs is within; the house of your body, well secured, but your wisdom remains outside and comes from your outside. Though it is the owner of your house, but your wisdom is like a journeyman, which comes and goes, as a result of which, your Nafs succeeds in dominating you. it is a dog which behaves like a lion in its house and street. Therefore, be careful to take the dog of your Nafs into the lion’s den, which is the nearness of a saintly master.

Mischiefs of the Nafs and body were not understood by the common people. They as well as the Nafs cannot be overcome without the inspirations from God, as happened when H. Dawood came in between. Everyone, similar to Nafs became a friend of the cow-owner, but not H. Dawood as he was a master. Only he is a master who has changed himself so much that he ceased to be in physical body of worldly demands, who as a result of his efforts was made by God as soul and heart in entirety.

H. Isa, son of Mariyam was running fast toward a hill as though a lion is after him for shedding his blood. A person followed him and said: “What is the matter? Nobody is after you, but you are running away with the speed of birds”.

But he was running so fast that he did not reply to him. After running for two more distances, he again called him out; asking him to stop for a moment for the sake of God as he wanted to know the reason, and he no more had the strength to run. He asked: “O generous one, you are running away from whom? Neither there a lion after you nor the fear of an enemy”. Jesus said: “I am running away from a fool. I want to get rid of him. Do not stop me!”
He said: “Are you not that Masiha who rids the deaf and blind of their sicknesses?”
He said: “Yes!” Then he said: “are you not that king who is the master of hidden miracle?

When you cast a spell on the dead body, it becomes alive and gets up like a ferocious lion”. He replied: “Yes! I am that one”. Then he said: “Do you not, O handsome, make birds from clay and then you blow softly upon them and instantly they become alive, and start flying:”? Jesus replied: “yes!”. Then he said: “Then, O clean spirit, you do whatever you want. Then what is it you are afraid of? With such evidence of your greatness, who in this world cannot be your follower?

sections.heading: Foolishness Is a Curse or Calamity
paras: Jesus said: “I swear upon that true, clear entity, God, who was the maker of the physical bodies in the beginning and is also the Creator of the soul. I swear upon the honour of His essence, and His clean Attributes (sifaat) for whom the heavens have torn their lapels. That spell and that Great Name (Ism-e-Aazam), that I recited upon the deaf and blind, made them healthy. I recited on hard rocky hill and it split and tore its own garment upon its navel. I read it over on a dead person and he got up with life. I recited upon non-existents; they came about as existents. But I recited on the heart of the foolish, not once, but a hundred thousand times, but it had no effect. On the contrary, he became harder like a rock and he did not give up his habits. He became like sand upon which nothing grows.”

That man asked: “What is the wisdom behind this that the great names had effect elsewhere but not on the foolish. That is a sickness and even this is a sickness here. It became a medicine there, and not here.”

Jesus said: “The sickness of foolishness is a calamity from God. The sickness of blindness is not a calamity. It is a trial. Trial is a sickness that brings about mercy; but foolishness is a sickness which causes injury. The sickness of foolishness injures the head, and that unfortunate fellow cannot be cured with mercy. It causes injury to others also. The seal that God has put on him cannot be removed by any effort.”

sections.heading: Run Away from the Foolish
paras: Run away from the foolish just as Jesus ran away. The company of the foolish has flowed much blood. Air steals away water little by little and the pond becomes dry in course of time. So also, the foolish steals you slowly and you get spoiled. He steals your heat of activities and wisdom and makes you cold and unfit, just as he keeps a stone slab underneath himself.

Christ’s running away was not out of fear. He was secured and sent to teach the people; but he ran away, to set an example for the followers. Even if the entire atmosphere becomes cold from horizon to horizon like the cold hydrosphere, the bright sun has nothing to fear. Whoever, possessing the warmth of the light of God, has no fear of the cold caused by rains.

chapters.title: Life Without Object
chapters.subtitle: Foolishness of the people of Sabaa and the advice of prophets to them and their refusal

paras: The story of the people of Sabaa came to my memory, for whom their foolish talk became a cause of contagious disease. That Sabaa was like a big city. You might have heard in the stories narrated for children. Though they are childish, yet there are many contents of wisdom. They say funny things in the stories; but you can search in them statements of wisdom as treasures are found in ruins.

Sabaa was a large city, but it’s worth was not as much of a earthen pot in God’s view. It was very large, very broad and long, with layers upon layers like the onion consisting of concentric layers of leaf bases. There was a population in it of ten cities, but all of them together were like three unworthy fellows. There were innumerable people of many types but were like three persons feeding upon improperly cooked food. Those who do not have an object of life are just like a half-developed men even if they are in thousands. One among them was blind fellow who claimed to see very far off objects. He could not see H. Sulaiman but boasted of seeing the feet of the ant. The other was deaf but claimed to hear even very low sounds with his sharp ears. He claimed to be aware of a great treasure even where there was not even a farthing worth of gold. There was another, naked and without any clothing’s, and a rider on a tiny, bony, sickly horse but claimed to wear garments with long lapels.
The blind fellow said: “I am seeing the armies of the enemies coming towards us. I can count their numbers and speak about the tribe they belong to.”
The deaf said: “I am hearing their sounds and decipher whatever they are talking about in both slow and loud tones”.
The naked fellow said: “I am afraid! They may not cut and take away the long lapel of my garment.”
The blind said: “They have come very close to us. Let us get up and run away from here before they overpower us.”
The deaf said: “Yes my friends! Their loud sounds are coming from a short distance. We should be careful”.
The naked fellow said: “Oh my lapel will be cut by their greed. I feel unprotected”.

They all left the city, and in a frightened mood entered into a village. They found there a fat fowl, and it contained no flesh but was only sick and forlorn. The blind saw it, the deaf heard its sound and the naked caught hold of it and covered it within its garment. The fowl was dry with the hitting’s of the beaks of a dead crow and its bones were weak like threads. They searched and found out and hurriedly took a pot which had no mouth and bottom. All the three of them kept the pot on a stove with all care and attention with the fat fowl in it. They cooked it so much and for so long, that the bones were fully cooked but the flesh was not seen. They ate it with pleasure as the lion eats its prey and all of them were belly filled like elephants. All of them swelled and became so fat like the large fat elephants: so fat and large that they could not be held in the entire world. With all this and their seven parts — head, chest, back, two hands, and two legs, they came out of the gap of the door.

sections.heading: The Invisible Path of Death
paras: The path of the death of creatures is a secret path. It is not visible, because it is not a tangible existing path. It is one belonging to the invisible, non-material non-existing path. Caravans are passing upon it one after another through the tiny gap of the door of death which is also invisible.

You cannot find this gap in the door if you search for it. The gap of the door is totally hidden, and it drags you very fast towards the next world through that invisible gap and only you will be alone just as one remains on the nuptial night only with his bride.

O Ziaul Huq Husamuddin, it is required that a detailed explanation is presented of this story. Know this my son, every short story is not a just a short story. It has lengthy meanings which will be known to those who have the capacity to know.

chapters.title: The Invisible Path of Death
chapters.subtitle: Explanation about the farsighted blind, sharp eared deaf and the long apparelled naked

paras: Consider the deaf as a man full of hope who heard about the news of our death but did not hear the message of his own death. He did not hear the steps of death and did not look at his transference from the world.

Greed is blind: He looks at hairs of all others and goes on speaking of the defects of others, in every street. His eyes do not see even a particle worth of his own defects, even though they are very keen in finding fault of others.
The naked fears that his lapel would be cut off; and how can this happen when he has no garment at all?

sections.heading: Fate of a Worldly Man
paras: The worldly man is a destitute of good deeds, yet he fears. One who does not possess anything need not fear of the thieves. That naked man came in the world naked and goes back from it with empty hands leaving everything here itself. But before going from here, he always has the fear of the thief as he possesses many things acquired between the birth and death. Hundreds of mourning’s and obituaries are made upon his death, but his soul laughs at itself for the false claims in obituaries and mournings as they are of no use for it. The rich man realises upon death that he has no wealth with him anymore; and every wise man also realises that he has gone without any possessions.

This is just like a child keeping pieces of earthen pots in his lap with great pleasure thinking of himself as very rich. If someone takes a piece from it, he cries and if it is returned, he feels pleased and laughs. As the child does not wear the dress of wisdom, his crying and laughing have no value in the view of others. A rich man also considers temporarily borrowed things as his own property. He also remains in anxiety to protect it. He is in constant fear of the thief that he may take away his possessions. Actually, he is dreaming in all these matters. If someone pulls his ear and wakes him up, he laughs at his fear of the thief.

sections.heading: Men of Wisdom and Learnings
paras: Similar is the fear of those wise and experts of sciences, who have worldly wisdom and knowledge. It is about such people that the Quran said: La ya’lamun: they do not know. Everyone is in the fear of thieves. Everyone thinks of his knowledge as great.

The man of worldly knowledge says that people by coming to him are wasting his time; but fails to see that he is himself wasting his time on useless knowledge. He says that people have no concern for his knowledge, even though his is held in useless matters from head to foot, like the naked man who fears that his lapel will be cut off and worries about the means of protecting his garment. He knows of thousands of benefits of his knowledge, but he does not know anything of himself. He knows the properties of everything and becomes like an ass about the affairs of his own soul. He proudly talks of the legitimates and illegitimates but does not know whether he is himself legitimate or not. He knows what is right and what is wrong. Think over as to whether you are yourself right or wrong. You know the worth and value of everything; but you do not know about your own worth and value. This is sheer foolishness. The astrologer talks of the auspicious and inauspicious time but does not know whether he is himself auspicious or not.

The spirit of all sciences is to know as to what will happen to him on the day of resurrection. The spirits of all sciences are that the knower should provide everlasting life to everyone. You have understood the fundamentals of the religion: its permissions and prohibitions about worldly matters but that is not enough. You should know about the fundamentals of your own self and of your own soul. It is better that one knows of the fundamentals of one’s own self and one’s soul. Therefore, O great man, know yourself.

chapters.title: Prosperity of Sabaa
chapters.subtitle: Prosperity of Sabaa and thanklessness of its people

paras: The fundamental base of the people of Sabaa was bad. They were very prosperous and happy, but they were ignorant of the ways by which they could maintain their prosperity. God had given them plenty of wealth, gardens and pasture lands from their left, and right. Fruits were so large in numbers on their trees that they fell on the roads creating obstacles for the passers-by. Roads and paths used to be full of fallen fruits putting the strangers in surprise. Their baskets were getting filled up with falling fruits without any trouble of plucking. Winds would blow in such a way as to fill the lapels of the passers-by. Branches of the trees full of fruits would come down due to their weight, kissing the heads and faces of the passers-by. The firemen in smelting units were wearing waist band of gold. Dogs were holding meat-pieces under their feet and wolfs in the forest suffered indigestion due to excessive eating. Cities and villages were safe from the onslaughts of thieves and wolves; and the sheep were not afraid of the fat wolves. Their dirty clothes were washed with the soap of burning fire within a short time. They would put their clothes in furnaces and take them back clean and washed. If I go on telling you about their comforts and pleasures, which were increasing day by day, I shall be prevented from telling other important things which the prophets brought for their guidance, as they had gone thankless to God. When their thanklessness went beyond limits, God’s honour started doing its acts.

chapters.title: Treatment of Spiritual Sickness
chapters.subtitle: Arrival of the Prophet with advice Wisdom vs Nafs (inner mischievous quality)

paras: Thirteen prophets came to them to guide them saying: “The grants for you are very much, be thankful for them to God. If your horse of thanksgiving has gone to sleep, wake it up. Even from rational point of view, giving thanks to the grantor is necessary as otherwise it will lead to permanent displeasure of the grantor. The grant of head requires that it should be placed in prostration; and of the legs in sitting down in prayer. Paying thanks by using the grants for the purpose they are granted, increases grants; and hundreds of flowers come out of the thorns”.

sections.heading: Refusal to Thank God
paras: The people said: “Our thanksgiving has been taken away by the devil; and we are deprived of it and disgusted of the comforts. We are so much disgusted of the grants that we feel pleasure neither in worship nor in sins. We do not want these grants and gardens; we do not need any means of prosperity, and prosperity itself. Grants have exhausted our needs. Please tell us, of what should we be thankful”. The prophets told them: “Your hearts are sick, as a result of which you are in a loss to realise the true path. The grants have become the causes of this sickness; a sick person does not get any energy from food. You are very obstinate. Many good things that came before you, became useless and their cleanliness turned into dirt. You have become an enemy of these pleasures, and whatever you lay your hands upon becomes displeasing. Even one known to you and your friend, appears unworthy and degraded to you; and those unknown to you become great and honourable. This is all due to the effect of your sickness, and its poison has spread among all the people. This sickness must be cured urgently as it makes sugar appear as dust. Every good thing that comes to you becomes bad, and even the water of life that gives eternal life becomes fire. This is a chemical that causes mental agony and death. At last, it makes your life itself as death. There are many foods which upon entering into bodies make life lively, but when they enter into your body, they become nauseating. There are many people who are loved by others; but those loved by you get disgraced.

When wisdom sincerely gets acquainted with wisdom, it develops into great friendship every moment. But when a mean Nafs (inner mischievous quality) goes closer to another such Nafs, the closeness gets reduced every moment. This is because one’s Nafs goes around only in its self-interest, which despoils the other’s Nafs. If you want to have a friend who should not be hated by you later, make friendship with wisdom and the wise. As you have fallen sick because of poisonous air, whatever you touch also becomes sick. If you hold a gem, it becomes stone and if you hold one with kindness, your kindness also becomes enmity. If you develop a new clean thought, it becomes tasteless and foul. The hearer will say: my friend, it is a very old idea; say something new. And if you further say ‘something newer, it will become more hateable than the earlier one.

sections.heading: Physicians Cure Physical Sickness and Spiritual Sickness Cured by Prophets
paras: As your sickness has become contagious, first get rid of it; and then even an old point becomes fresh one for you. New meanings will start coming to your mind. This old point will sprout fresh leaves on twigs, and even from the roots new points will come about.

The prophets further said: We are physicians, and disciples of the Great Lord. When the Mediterranean Sea looks at us it splits as it did by looking at H. Musa. There are different kinds of physicians who look at the conditions of your physical heart by touching your pulse. But we look at the conditions of the spiritual heart through our deeply hidden spiritual intelligence. They see the physical heart for physical sickness; we see the spiritual heart for its sickness. They prescribe medicines through foods and fruits to cure the animal soul and through it the physical body. But we prescribe medicines through our own words and actions, which we are instructed to by spiritual inspiration from the light of God. We tell you that this act is profitable and that the other separates you from the right path. This word from us advances you forward and that one acts as a sting and causes harm. This is like this, and that is like that; this is good and that is bad. We keep all this before you and very clearly exhibit to you. You may follow this and follow that. Poison and sugar, and gem and stone are clearly demonstrated before you. Those physicians bring forth rational arguments, but our argument is the inspiration from God. We do not seek any remuneration from anybody, and we get very great renumeration from God. Hear us! Our medicine is for incurable sores and it is for all types of sicknesses: (as stated in the Quran: la as’alakum alaihi ajran: I ask of you no reward for this: Huud: 11: 51.)

chapters.title: Demand of Miracles
chapters.subtitle: Peoples seeking of miracles from prophets

paras: People challenged the prophets saying! “O claimants of prophethood! Who is the witness for your profitable treatment of sicknesses and knowledge? You are also bound by the same conditions of eating and sleeping as we are. Become like us and enjoy in the fields. You are also made up of clay and water and bound by them like us. How can you be the catchers of the hearts like seemurgh (a fictional bird found in Caucasus mountains)? [ such a challenge was put before the noble Prophet of Islam as stated in the Quran: maalihzaalrasuli yukulut tua’ama wa yamshi fil aswaq: what sort of an apostle is this who eats food and walks through the streets: Furqan 25: 7]. Your desire for grand status and leadership induces you to consider yourselves among the prophets. We do not like this kind of boastfulness and falsehood. We do not want to hear you and slip into mean places.”

The prophets said: “Those statements of yours are due to your sickness. The capital of blindness is a curtain against sighting. You have heard our claim, but you do not see the gems in our hands. These gems are a trail for the people, which we are turning around their eyes to see. The very question about the evidence itself is an evidence of the fact that he is not seeing the gems, establishing the fact that he is a victim of blindness. Sun has risen and is asking you to rise up saying, the day has come about, and do not disagree. You can see it plainly if you ask the sun to give the evidence of its coming, it will tell you to pray to God to give you eyes. One who searches for a lamp to see during daytime, makes an announcement of his blindness that he is not seeing the sunlight. If you do not see, at least you should suspect that day has come, and you are behind the curtain. Do not reveal your blindness through such talk, be silent and wait for God’s grace. Perhaps, a grace without seeking anything in return may come, which may turn your heart away from this misfortune. Otherwise, you will be in blindness for ever and your mirror will go under thick blankets of darkness. Asking for showing the day during daytime, puts you in great disgrace. You become a laughingstock. Patience and silence attract and absorb mercy of others, of their won, and seeking an evidence for this is a sickness”.

Hold on to the command “pay heed” so that you may receive the reward of paying heed from God as stated in Quran: wa izaa qurial quranu, fa astamilahu va ansitu la allakum turhamun: And when the Quran is recited, give ear to it and pay heed, that you may obtain mercy: (Al a’raaf 7: 204). If you do not want the sickness to come back, you may fall down before the prophets. Sell out your excessive talk and sacrifice life, status and wealth, so that God’s graces may speak out your praises to such an extent that the heavens may feel jealous of you. If you keep a watch on the hearts of the physicians of the soul, you will see everything in clarity and feel like repenting on your acts. Elimination of this blindness is not in the hands of people, but honouring these physicians is the proper means for it. Be a slave with all your heart of these physicians, so that you may receive the fine fragrance of musk and ambergris.

chapters.title: Refusal to Heed Advice
chapters.subtitle: People’s accusations on the prophets

paras: The people said: “All this is treacherous talk. How can God make Tom, Dick and Harry as His representatives? The messenger of a king ought to be a king. Where is water and mud of which men are made and the Creator of heavens? Have we eaten the brain of the donkey that we should consider mosquitoes like you to be equal to Huma (the legendary bird upon the falling of whose shadow upon someone, he would become a king). Where is huma, where is mosquito, mud and God? What has a particle to do with the sun? What kind of relations are these, which cannot enter into the mind and strike at wisdom? How long do you talk of this nonsense? What kind of treachery, cheating and treason is this? Where is He, where is this sky and this raw thread? Our wisdom does not accept these stories. If not much, we certainly have this much wisdom to differentiate between carrot and karras (foul smelting lengthy fruits).

chapters.title: Rabbit Fooled Elephants
chapters.subtitle: Story of the rabbits who sent one of them as messenger of moon to the elephants to avoid going to the pond, as is mentioned in the book — Kalila and Damna

paras: They said: “What you say is like what a rabbit said that he was a messenger and friend of the moon. This he did as all flocks of forest animals were in great trouble because of the coming of large number of elephants to the pond with clean water. They were all, out of fear of the elephants, away from the ponds. As they were all weak, they decided to keep the elephants away by means of a trick. An old rabbit gave a call from the top of the hill to the elephants on a new moon night: He said: “O king of the elephants! I am a messenger. Stand up before me. Restrictions, anger and threats are not worthy of being put upon messenger. Moon is telling the elephants: “Go away from the pond as it is my property; as otherwise I shall turn you all blind.” I have given this message to you and I have performed my duty. Leave this pond and go away so as to remain protected from my sword. The proof of what I say is that the moon gets disturbed with the drinking of water by the elephants. O king of elephants! Come to the pond on the fourteenth night so as to witness its truth. Come over on that night and witness the proof.”

After fourteen days the king of the elephant came over to the pond, when the moon was fully bright. It inserted its trunk in water and the water started waving and the moon also appeared to be shaking. The elephant upon the shaking of moon got convinced, frightened and ran away. After this, no elephant came to the pond.
After narrating this story, the people of Sabaa said: We are not fools like the elephants to be frightened by the shaking of the moon.

chapters.title: Guided and the Misguided
chapters.subtitle: Prophets reply to the people with an example

paras: The prophets said: “Regrettable, it is O fools! Our advice has hardened further your shackles. Regrettable, that due to your sickness, medicine has become poison for your life. A lamp increases the darkness of the eyes, when God puts a curtain of wrath on them. What leadership do we expect from you? When our leadership is higher than the sky due to our nearness with God. What honour can a sea full of pearls get from a ship. And in particular, in your case the ship is full of filth. So regrettable for that eye that is blind and dark which sees the sun as a particle.

It is like the case of Iblis whose eye saw the unique and unmatchable Adam as nothing more than mud. His mad eyes showed the spring season of Adam’s greatness as autumn and took him to the place that he deserved. Many a times, it happens that many fortunes that come after lapses of time, turn back on the way from an unfortunate fellow. Many a times beautiful beloveds come over to strangers who do not know, what love is. Similarly, sometimes wealth goes to such fellows who do not know its worth. Why are the foolish deprived of the wealth of wisdom; and the misguided of the right ways? It is our misfortune that makes the eyes see wrong things and turn our hearts from the right to wrong decisions.

sections.heading: Tails Follow the Heads
paras: When an idol made of stone has become an object of your worship, curse and blindness have become your sunshades. How could your stone, be able to become a partner of God and why did not your wisdom and soul become secret bearers of God. When a dead mosquito became one lie the Huma, why not a living man be a secret bearer of angels. That lifeless idol is sculptured by you out of stone and the mosquito full of life is made by God. Everybody loves his creations and takes care of them. Tail of the snake follows its head taking it as its religious duty. Neither the tail has any wealth and grace in it, nor the head provides any relief and pleasure. Yet the tail moves around the snake’s head and goes wherever the head goes. Both of them are very good and devoted friends of each other.

sections.heading: All Things Appropriately Made
paras: That wiseman Sanaai from Ghazni has said the same in his book “Ilahi Nama” (God’s message), if you can carefully go through. He has said: “Do not talk much in what God has ordained. Your talk will amount to nonsense. He has made the donkey’s ears suiting to its body. Bodies and parts of the body are proportionately and appropriately made; and their qualities are made in accordance with the souls. Quality of every soul suits to itself and certainly other things are made to accord with it. (Like: when a soul is created for rejection of God (Kufr), kufr only suits to its quality). When the quality of the soul goes nearby to its taste, it adopts it and values it as its face and eyes. Good and bad are created to suit the respective qualities, and whatever has been written by God is appropriate. Eyes and hearts of men are between his two fingers, just as the pen in the hands of a writer; and they turn in whatever manner He wants. There is one finger of love and another of wrath; and the tips of these fingers are decided for contraction or expansion of the heart.

You should always keep the majesty of God and think as to in which of the two fingers you are. All your wishes and actions are under the command of these fingers. The difference between yourself and others will be known at the crossroad of the doomsday, as both cross over each other. The changes of the situations that take place in your heart are also the products of His writings and scorings. That is to say: Wishing and cancelling of wishes are all according to His wishing and cancelling. (Some great men have said that they understood their Lord in the cancellation of their desire). But we do not know what is written, being written and being scored off by the movements this pen. Therefore, the only way of keeping ourselves in satisfaction lies in our total submission, entreating and praying to God. Your heart knows the good and bad of matters of its own, but only to the extent of its capacity”.

Be that as it may, we have been hanging on to the story of the rabbit and elephant as though the rabbit is comparable to the prophets and the people of Sabaa to elephants, by mingling of eternal wisdom of God with the human reasons in worldly affairs.

chapters.title: No Competence to Exemplify
chapters.subtitle: To explain that everyone cannot exemplify on matters, especially in relation to God

paras: What right did the people of Sabaa had to present an example as they did to compare the rabbit to prophets and themselves to elephant, while talking about the clear matters of God. The right to give example exclusively belongs to those who have the knowledge of the unseen and the capacity to explain. You cannot explain the secrets of the (magical powers) of the tufts and beautiful cheeks so long as you are not bald, (especially a bald woman). H. Musa looked at the staff as staff only, but it was not so. It was a python, and this could be known only when it opened its mouth. When such a great king did not know the secret of wood, what can you know of the secrets of the nets spread over and the grains thereon to catch the birds. When H. Musa’s eyes were wrong in the example, what can you with your worth as of a rat, blabber about and penetrate into the depths of knowledge to cite an example. (as the worthless people of Sabaa did).

Any example you give will become like a python and will tear you to pieces. The accursed Satan brought out an example when directed by God to prostrate to Adam. He said: “You created me with fire and Adam with mud: “(khalaqtani min naarin wa khaqtahu min teen: (Aa’raaf 7: 12). For this he has remained accursed till the doomsday.

sections.heading: What Happened to Qaruun?
paras: Qaruun, (as stated to be Korah in the English Bible) was one of the tribe of Musa. He was given so much of wealth by God that the very keys of it were a burden to the body of a strong camel. His people told him not to be proud of wealth as God does not love the proud, and to do good and not to seek mischief in the world. But he arrogantly said that this wealth was given to him because of a certain knowledge which he had. As stated in the Quran: innama uutituhu alla ilmin: (Qasas: 28: 78). The result of this arrogance was that he was thrust into the earth with all his wealth, throne and crown as stated in the Quran: fakhasafna bihi wa bilaarihil ardh: then, We caused the earth to swallow up him and his house: (Qasas: 28: 81).

sections.heading: Nimrod’s Arrogance and End
paras: This case comes from the incident of Nimrod, king of Babylonia during the days of H. Ibrahim, who had claimed Godly power. He had disputed with H. Ibrahim as he was granted power by God. In the course of arguments, H. Ibrahim spoke of the might of God saying that God has power over life and death. He arrogantly said: I give life and death: Anaa uhyi wa umituu: (Al Baqara: 2: 258). Upon this Ibrahim said: God causes sun to rise from the East, you may do so from west. This confounded him. Subsequently a mosquito entered into his head through his nose and his end came with the tearing of his brain.

sections.heading: Phaeraoh’s Case
paras: Phaeraoh exhibited similar arrogance as a result of which he was drowned into water and got destroyed. It happened when H. Musa left Egypt with his followers and Phaeraoh followed them. And when the Nile (or Mediterranean Sea) came on the way, H. Musa struck on water with his staff and the water split paving the way for Bani Israil to pass through and they reached the bank on the other side. Phaeraoh also followed them and when he reached the middle of the split water, water re-joined drowning him into it.

Similar case came to the community of ‘Aad; and became an example of destruction for arrogance; and there was such a strong wind on them that they and their houses fell upside down, and they all dried, resulting in their bones getting smashed to pieces.

Every unfortunate mean fellow brought examples for God and fell upside down in the depths of hell. You may consider their examples like owls and crows (which people believe as causes of misfortune)! hundreds of families have been destroyed.

chapters.title: Exemplification of People
chapters.subtitle: Citing of example by the community of Noah while he was building up the Ark

paras: H. Noah made a ship (Noah’s Ark) in the forest. Hundreds of citers of examples came over to make fun of him telling he is making a ship in a forest where there is neither water nor a well. What an ignorant fool he is! One said to sail the ship and another to fix feathers and wings to it to fly. Another said: its tail is curved (set it right). Another said: its back is curved. One would ask where its saddle is, and another: why are its legs turned backward. Another would say: O its goatskin is empty, and another would say: what for is this donkey? Another would say: perhaps you have no work to do, or you have lost your mental balance, or you have gone mad.
But Noah simply used to say: This is as per the command of God. This is not going to lose its worth by your nonsensical talks.

chapters.title: Truth Is Known Later
chapters.subtitle: Story of the thief who was asked as to what he was doing near a wall at midnight; and his saying: I am beating drum

paras: A mischievous cunning thief was digging a pit in the foundation of a wall. A sickly, half-asleep man was hearing the sound of digging. He went on the roof, bent down his head and asked him as to what he was doing at this dead of the night and who he was. He replied: “O elderly gentleman, I am beating a drum”.

He said: “This is a different sound than that of a drum”. He said: “The real sound can be heard by you tomorrow morning. It will be a sound of ‘alas’ and ‘woe unto me’. You will hear the sound of the drum after my going away: and you will know of the entirety and its parts”.

O the fellows who cited the example of the rabbit and elephants: you are half-baked fellows. You have fallen in great wrongs. Become fully developed in the fire of truth and be safe. The example you have cited is petty, croocked and misleading. You are such that you cannot even know how it is crooked and misleading.

chapters.title: Wrong Examples Mislead
chapters.subtitle: Reply to the example of the rabbit cited by the rejectors

paras: Know the secret of the example of the rabbit, O incompetent devil, which came to you as a messenger before your nafs (inner mischievous self) and deprived your foolish nafs of the water of life which Khizr drank and became immortal. You have reversed the meanings, spoken of rejections of truth and therefore prepare yourself for punishment. (You have compared the treacherous rabbit to prophets). You have called the moon to be disturbed in clear water, through which the rabbit frightened the elephants. You narrate the story of rabbit, elephant and water and the fright of the elephants due to the disturbance of the moon and compared moon with God. O blind fellows, what comparison can it have with that moon (God) to whom all big and small are obedient.

sections.heading: Everything: Obedient to God
paras: Everything: the moon, sun, sky, wisdom, life and angels — all obey Him. What to say of them, wild animals, birds, rocks, kings, beggars and emperors; cities, mountains, oceans all obey Him. Come to times: months, years, days and nights obey Him. All elements: earth, water, fire and air are obedient to Him: Come to seasons — winter, summer, autumn and spring are all obedient to Him like the ball is under the movements of the bat. He is the son of the sun of the sun. What nonsense am I talking about? Perhaps I am in sleep! I am wrong in comparing God with the Sun. he is absolutely uncomparable.

sections.heading: Destruction of Mischief Mongers by Prophets
paras: O you lowly-based-people of Sabaa! Thousands of cities have been overturned with the wrath of these kings (prophets). Mountains break into a hundred pieces. The sun is revolving around, like the donkey tied to the water wheel. The wrath of the men of God dries up the clouds. Their anger destroys the worlds. O dead bodies unsmeared with fragrance, look at torture chamber of Sodom, the city of Lot, (that was shattered to dust with rocks and stones). What is an elephant’s might: a few birds (Ababils) flying in the air broke apart their bones, which had accompanied king Abraha of Abyssinia when he wanted to demolish the Ka’aba at Makka? Ababils are some of the weakest among the birds, but they tore the elephants in such a manner that, they could not be patched. Who has not heard of the deluge during the lifetime of Noah; or of the battle between the Phaeraoh’s army and the angels? The spirits of the angles defeated and drowned them in water, in which they were dissolved like particles. Who has not heard of the incidents of the Th(s)amud, who were flown like dust by the winds?

sections.heading: Pretention of Not Seeing and Pleading Ignorant
paras: Now turn your eyes towards those men, mighty like elephants, who destroyed the elephants in the battles. They are the cruel kings mighty like elephants, who were constantly hit by the stones with the wraths of the hearts. They are moving about in darkness, without getting any sympathy and mercy from anyone. You seem to have not heard of such famous and infamous fellows. Everyone has seen them, but you appear to have not seen, what you have, in fact, seen. Wait for some time. Death will open up your eyes fully. Even though both the worlds are brightened with the sun and other lights, but you are moving about in darkness like the blind. You are deprived of that great light of that Moon and your windows are shut at that. You have left the large palace and fallen into the narrow well. There is no fault on the part of the great and wide worlds. How can that soul look at the face of H. Yusuf, which is under the clutches of wolfishness. The songs of H. Dawood reach the lifeless rocks and hills, but the ears of these stone-hearted fellows cannot hear them. Great honour to wisdom and justice, as God knows very well as to and at what times they should prevail.

sections.heading: Versus in Arabic
paras: O the people of Sabaa, believe in the prophets. Believe in the spirit which has been imprisoned and also imprisons. Believe in them who are the raisers of the sun, who will protect you from disgrace on the doomsday. Believe in them who are bright moons, well before you, and meet them on doomsday. They are the lamps in darkness. Honour them who are the keys of hope. Believe in them, who do not expect any wealth from you. Do not be in misguidance and do not look at those not known to you.

Your raise an objection that, I speak in Arabic and we do not know Arabic, see I have spoken in Persian. Whether you are a slave or the beautiful Turk: all are made up of water and mud. Forget all this and hear what all the prophets have said about God. Fall in love with them not with Arab, Persian or Turk. There are two methods of taking lessons. Take lessons from past events or take instructions of the prophets, and fly on carefully toward the final end.

chapters.title: Versus in Arabic
chapters.subtitle: Meaning of precaution and the man with precaution

paras: What is pre-caution? It is maintaining mediocrity in respect of two opposite things. Adopt that way which keeps you away from mental agony. One tells you that the destination comes after seven days; and there is no water available on the way and the road also has burning sand. The other one says: “It is wrong. You will see plenty of flowing streams”. Precautions in this situation is that you should carry water so as, not to face difficulty. If there is water on the way, flow away your water. It is no good to argue on this matter. [This is the precaution one has to follow in respect of the risks involved on the doomsday. If what is stated about it, is just a story as stated by many, it is better to carry good deeds in the baggage, instead of going empty handed. If what is stated is true, one is saved; and if it is not, a great calamity is avoided of its own. This is the advice that H. Ali had given to a non-believer —Qazi Sajjad Hussain].

sections.heading: What Satan Did with H. Adam?
paras: O men, the children of Adam the great vicegerent of God! Be wise and take precaution for the doomsday. The enemy of yours, Satan had played great mischief with Adam, your grandfather, by taking him from the highest of the high places (illiyyin) and dragged him into this prison of the world. He defeated the king from the chess board, took him away from paradise and put him into difficulties. He gripped around some of his strong muscles and defeated him in the bout and put him to shame. He has done such acts with that strong wrestler. Do not take him to be worthless.

sections.heading: Results of Adam’s Falling into Satan’s Trap
paras: That jealous fellow took away the crown and garments of our parents with treachery. He made them naked, disgraced and lowly. For this, Adam wept for years so much, that grass grew from the place where his tears fell. He was sorry for his fate, that such a tragical situation was written in the scroll of his acts. You may consider the cleverness of Satan that he plucked the hairs of Adam’s beard which are directly under his eyes and so near to him as against other hairs. O worshipers of clay! Take care of the Satan’s mischief and strike the sword of la howla (there is no power) upon him to make him say that there is no power and strength in anybody except in God.

sections.heading: Do Not Be Greedy
paras: He looks at you from hidden places, which cannot be seen by you. Hunters always spread grains, which are visible, and not the net. Be cautious of every place where you see grains, so as not be caught in the trap. Fly off far far away O pigeon, from the grain, because as soon as you pick the grain, you are caught. That bird which ignores the sight of grain, gets unlimited quantities of grains from the forest. The man who runs away from the grains of pleasures spread over by the devil has got ready for him the flowers in the garden of purity. He remains satisfied with the possessions that he keeps for himself free from the clutches of the devil.

chapters.title: Do Not Repeat Mistakes
chapters.subtitle: Tragedy of the Bird that gave up precaution due to greed

paras: Know about the bird that was sitting on a wall, which kept its eyes on the grains and net. It looked toward the forest for once, and then turned toward the grains before it. It compared and weighed both of its sights and suddenly gave up the sight of wisdom. It flew, picked the grain and got trapped. The hunter caught it, slaughtered it and ate it and finished it for ever.

There was another bird which gave up its anxieties, turned its sight from the grain and flew toward the forest. Its feathers and wings were beautiful, and it became a leader of the other birds. Whichever bird becomes its follower gets delivered and occupies a place of peace and freedom. Because its heart was one of precaution, it became, their king and the garden became its destination. It was happy with it.

sections.heading: Repentance and Forgetfulness
paras: When you have to deal with any matter, do as this bird did. Many a times you get trapped in the net of greed and allow your throat to slit. Then, that great Forgiver, God, releases you, by accepting your repentance. He accepts your repentance and releases you. He says: We turn in the direction in which you turn. We have linked the reward of jobs with the jobs done. When you bring one of a couple, the other one of the couple follows it. The couples always go together. When someone catches a male, its female goes in search of the male.

But after the acceptance of your repentance when you are released, you throw dust into the eyes of acceptance and commit the mistake again. The Acceptor of repentance again releases you and warns you be careful. Do not commit the mistake again. But when the Commander of forgetfulness sends His message, you are once again dragged into fire. This is like the moth which again and again falls on the fire. O moth do not fall into forgetfulness and doubts. Look at your burnt-out wings.

sections.heading: Thanking Forgiveness by Not Repeating Mistake
paras: When you happened to be saved, you should be thankful by not going toward the grain again. When you give your thanks in this way, He will grant you more of such food which is without the fear of your enemy and of the net. You should always remember the grant of release from the net given to you. Many a times when you are caught in difficulties and pain, you pray to God to save you from these, so that you would render such service and benevolence to others, that you would bury the eyes of the devil in mud. When God gave you relief and release, you behave in the same way as you behaved earlier. You forgot everything and made yourself careless and unconscious.

chapters.title: Thanksgiving Increases Grants
chapters.subtitle: Decision of the Dogs during winter to build houses in summer for next winter

paras: The bones of dogs cluster together during winter due to the chill. They become thin. The dog takes a decision that its body should be made hard enough like a stone. When summer arrives, it will make a house of stones, on the hope that its bones expand and his body swells. But after its body becomes fat in summer it forgets the past experience of winter and it stretches its legs and lies down under a shade, lazy, bellyful, forgetful and arrogant. Looking at its body it says to itself that its fat body cannot occupy any house. Its past experience tells it to make a house, but it questions about the house that can accommodate its fat body.

This is how man also behaves, when he is in troubles. His bones become brittle and get scattered and he decides that he will make a home of repentance, so as to get comforts thereafter. When troubles pass off, his greed becomes stronger and fat as in the case of the dog and his decision to make a house for future vanishes.

sections.heading: Thanking Itself Is a Grant
paras: Thanksgiving upon the receipt of grants is greater than the grants. One who rides fast on the horse of thanksgiving does not feel any torture. Thanksgiving is the soul of grants and grant is like the body, because in order to give thanksgiving, you are taken by it to the grantor’s house. Pleasures of grants bring about carelessness, but thanksgiving warns and activates you. By thanksgiving you get more grants from the Grantor, for God has said: wa lain shakertum la’azidanna kum (if you are grateful, I will add more favours unto you: (Ibrahim: 14: 7). As thanksgiving in your mind, itself is a great grant of God, by resorting to thanksgiving, you become further rich and great so to become one to grant those who are lesser in possessions and in need. You will have plenty of food and tasty dishes to such an extent that you will have no worry for getting food and knocking the door of anyone else than God. Be always thankful to the grants of God, the greatest Grantor, as otherwise, plenty of grants will make you arrogant and headlong. Thanking drags many more grants, and the one who disregards God’s grants becomes an infidel.

chapters.title: Arguments of Predestinarians
chapters.subtitle: Preventing the prophets from advice by the rejectors, and bringing forward arguments of the pre-destinarians and speaking of nonsense

paras: The people of Sabaa said: “O too-much of advice-givers, enough of your advice. What all you said would have been enough if there were people in this place with free will as their belief, to take their own decisions. God has put a seal on our hearts, and nobody can proceed on more than what God has provided. That Great painter has made our picture in such a way that it cannot change by any amount of persuasion. Every act of ours and of everything is predestined by God, and nobody can alter it. If you tell an ordinary stone to become a ruby for a hundred years, or tell something to an old thing to become new, or tell dust to become water, or tell water to become honey or milk, or tell the fire not to be fire, and become only light, tell a mosquito to go toward the air, or tell a counterfeit to become genuine, alchemy and acidic, they shall never give up their features. They shall continue to be as they are.

sections.heading: Properties of Things Do Not Change
paras: How can water become honey, my honourable sir. The Creator of the heavens and its inhabitants; of water, earth and dust, has established certain features for all. He has put the heavens in clear and automatic rotation. He has provided water and clay to pollute each other to produce plants. Heavens cannot get polluted; and water and clay cannot become pure of each other. Everything is allotted a path to proceed upon and by any amount of your efforts a mountain cannot become a scrap of grass”.

chapters.title: Permanent and Temporary Features
chapters.subtitle: Reply of Prophets to Predestinarians

paras: The prophets said: “Yes, God has created such qualities, from which you cannot turn away your face. He has also created some temporary qualities, which sometimes, become acceptable and sometimes rejectable. The same unacceptable qualities later change into acceptable ones. Telling a stone to become gold is non-sense, but if the same is told to copper to become gold, it can become. If you tell sand to become flowers, it cannot, but clay can become flowers. He has created certain diseases for which there is no treatment like deafness, flat nose and blindness. But there are diseases for which there are treatments like paralysis and headache. Medicines are created to eliminate sicknesses. These sicknesses and medicines are not illogical. Rather, generally there is a medicine for sicknesses; but generally, there are medicines for sicknesses. If you put efforts, you can know them.

chapters.title: Incurable Diseases
chapters.subtitle: Further arguments by pre-destinarians

paras: The people of Sabaa countered: “Even if medicines can cure diseases, our disease is such, which cannot be cured. You may see yourself: for years together, you have spoken to us of these instructions and spells, but at each time the sickness has increased. If our sickness were one to be cured by medicine, at least a little of it would have gone. But it has not happened. When a knot develops in the passage to liver, water does not reach it, causing continuing thirst. Even one drinks a river of water, it goes elsewhere. The thirst is not quenched; but on the contrary it causes swelling of the limbs. Water ceases to be of any use”.

chapters.title: Soul Not Bound by Space
chapters.subtitle: Prophets further, arguments to predestinarians

paras: The prophets said: “Giving up hopes is bad. There is no limit to God’s graces and mercies. It is not proper to lose hope from such a great benevolent. Put your hands into the hunting bag of that great benefactor. There are many jobs which are very difficult in the beginning, but later on, become easy, and difficulties go away. Even after dejection, there are possibilities of many hopes, just as the sun appears after dark night. We admit that you have become hard like stones and you have put locks on your ears and hearts. But we do not have anything but to obey God. Our job is only to accept His command and work on it. He has given us the command to do this, and what we say is not our saying. It is only as per His. We live only to obey Him. If He tells us to sow seeds in sand, we do it. We are only passing God’s command to you.

sections.heading: Prophets: Obedient Servants of God
paras: Prophets do not have any friend other than God. The people’s acceptance or rejection of the message is of no concern for us. The labour of the conveyance of the messages is paid by Him. We have become ugly in the view of the enemies because of our love for the Friend. We are not tired in the path of the Friend’s abode. We never get stranded on the way. Only that person gets dejected and tired, who is in a prison being separated from friend.

“Our beloved is always with us, and his benevolences are upon us continuously and we are even thankful for this. There are gardens in our hearts, which do not have the fear of becoming old and getting dried up. They are always fresh, youthful, sweet, laughing and pleasing. A moment and a century are the same for us; and length and width have no distinction for us. Length and breadth are the property of material bodies; but are not those of the souls.

sections.heading: Time and Space Not for Soul
paras: Three hundred and nine years (309 of the people of the cave (ashab-e-kahaf) were like one day without pain and troubles. And when they woke up, it was not even one day but a few moments when their souls having gone into the world of non-existence came back and re-entered into their bodies. When days and nights; and months and years are the same for the soul which is not bound by space and time, it has no sense of becoming hungry, getting fed, tired and old. In the gardens of the world of spirits, selfness does not exist and there is only a state of loss of senses, and that is due to the drinks provided by the large cups of the benevolence of God. This is not a case of one who has neither tasted nor seen. He cannot understand, just as the fragrance of rose is not understandable by the insects in cow dung. What is stated here is not imagination, as if it were so it would have been completely lost. How can the hell imagine of the paradise? This is like the dirty pig’s face, which cannot make anyone beautiful. Similarly, people of this world cannot understand the intoxication of that world.

Therefore, considering yourselves to be great, O people of Sabaa, do not tear your throats by loud shouting. We have brought that morsel of heavenly food up to your mouths: do take it. We have undergone great troubles to get those Informations and provide them to you without efforts on your side. Whoever follows us, gets delivered of the torture of fire, and gets into the paradise. And those who do not take our advice get into eternal torture. Take the opportunity to find out the path of prosperity, through the stars of fortune, because, as of now, you are in a dark, deep well.

chapters.title: Prophets Considered Inauspious
chapters.subtitle: People’s further objections to reject the advice

paras: The people said: “You may consider yourselves to be very noble, and prosperous, but we consider you to be unfortunate, our opponents and rejectors. We were not having any kind of worries, and you have put us in tensions and troubles. You have spoiled the taste of our pleasure of unity and common thinking in us, and your unsavoury predictions have brought about hundreds of separations. We were like parrots enjoying tasty food and sugar, but you made us into birds frightened of death. All stories of tragedies, narrations of viciousness, prediction of misfortunes, discussions of alterations of fate, tortures and imprisonments, are all products of your exemplifications and misapprehension and due to your desire to increase sorrows.

chapters.title: Difference Between Good and Vicious
chapters.subtitle: Reply of the prophets AS

paras: The prophet said: What is foretold, good and bad receives support from your own souls. If you are sleeping in a dangerous place and a python comes over to swallow you, noble man wakes you up to run away fast. You tell him that he is making a bad omen. In such a circumstance, it is not calling him bad that helps, but opening your eyes to see the danger, and know what a bad omen is. I am ridding you of this danger and taking you to your house as a prophet is informed of hidden things, as he sees things which other worldly people do not see.

“If a physician tells you not to eat a raw grape as it would cause sickness, you ask him as to why he makes a wrong forecast. You consider an adviser to be sinful. An astrologer tells you not to volunteer to do some job as it is an inauspicious time, so that you may not be harmed and deprived, you accept his advice even though you find him to be wrong on a hundred occasions and right on only two. Our forecasting has never been wrong, yet it is not acceptable to you. The physicians and astrologers speak on speculations, but we do on the basis of observations.

We see smoke and fire from a distance which is about to reach the rejectors; and you tell us to keep quiet as these are forecasts which put you into loss. You do not take the advice of advisers. Wherever you go, your ill feelings will accompany you.

A python is moving behind you and someone from the roof of his house sees this and warns you; and you tell him: do not say this and cause worries to me. That well-wisher will tell you to be happy, and the matter ends. When the python hits upon your face, all your happiness turns sour. Then you will tell him: “You should have torn my clothes, lamented upon me and told me. You should have hit my head with a stone, so as to make this havoc visible to me”.
He would reply:” I did not want you to be sorrowful”. Then you would say: “As if you have made me happy now”.

He would say:” I was gentlemanly in advising you, so that you might be relieved of this calamity. You behaved in a mean manner. With your meanness, you did not value my words and considered my warnings as harmful and made a capital of your rebellious mood”.

sections.heading: Nature of the Mean Fellows
paras: This is the nature of the mean fellows. If you do good to them, they will do bad to you. Your (inner mischievous self) is the meanest of all. Nafs (inner mischievous self) has to be weakened through (denial) as it is mean, and goodness does not suit its nature. If you do good to the good people, they will repay you with seven hundred good things. But a mean fellow can be your faithful slave only if you keep him under troubles and deprivation. The infidels commit atrocities if they are full of grants and their call for grace will be only in the hell, when they would say: “O our Lord”. Mean fellows remain honest when in troubles; and when they see goodness, they commit torture.

chapters.title: Places of Worship of the Good and Bad
