Aulia see dreams even when they are awake and enter into the world of spirits and intangibles which has no doors. But what they see is not a dream. What they see is real.

H. Bilal said: “My house is narrow, and my life is crippled in it. I have destroyed this house to build a royal palace there. I am crippled in the world just as a baby is twisted in the womb. I have completed the period of nine months and I have to be moved out of the uterus. If my mother does not feel labour pain, I would continue to be in this hell-like-prison. The mother of my instinct pain of her death to deliver my soul in this is in the pain of its death and delivers me in this world just like the delivery of the baby of the goat, so that it may feed upon an evergreen garden. That is to say that the pain occurs upon the body, but the soul gets released. This release of soul is necessary to fatten it in the wide world after breaking the walls of the prison of the womb. Mother cries out of the labour pain and says: save from the pain; but the baby laughs upon getting his freedom as though he says give me a place of safety.

sections.heading: People Are Generally Ignorant
paras: Everything that exists under the sky has its mother, be it among animals, plants or minerals. Everyone is unaware of the pains of others, excepting those who are well informed and wise. A wise man with a trimmed short beard knows about the houses of others (wise men keep short beards), but the one with a long beard does not know about himself. (Foolish people generally keep long beards). The former is like the saints and the latter are like the fool ignorant of themselves. The men of heart know about the affairs of others so well that they themselves would not know. Therefore, my elderly friend, if you are not wise and well informed, you do not know about yourself. The men of heart see all that is written on your forehead. Therefore, feel shy of yourself as you do not know yourself.

chapters.title: Soul and Wisdom Are Not Matter, Space and Time
chapters.subtitle: All heedlessness, laziness and ignorance are due to the body as it is lowly and earthly

sections.heading: Smokey and Lightly Knowledge
paras: Heedlessness was the act of the body when it got life and soul, even upon seeing the secrets with certainty. Knowledge did not provide it with care and concern for work. Certain acts occur in the body even without intention, which also it does not heed. If the earth goes out of its place in the space, there will be no night, no shadow, night or a place for the shadow to fall. It is due to the earth and not due to heavens or the moon. Smoke is connected with fuel and not with the brightness giving flame. Uncertain inclinations of the heart are like smoke, and they put one in mistakes and wrongs, but wisdom which is like brightness takes toward clarity and certainty. All heaviness of the body and laziness are due to the body, but soul is weightless, and it flies higher and higher. Redness of the face is due to excess of blood; paleness is due to the movement of yellow bile, whiteness is due to strength of phlegm, and blackness is due to black bile. Just as these things are caused by differences of colours, impurities are caused into the soul by some causes, as otherwise it is a bright substance.

sections.heading: Cause and Effect: Demonstrative, Not Real
paras: The real fact is that the effects, symbols and marks are caused by the Creator, but those who go by the materials (materialists) do not see anything other than cause and effect. Pulp that is not separated from the rind cannot escape dependence upon the physician and sickness. That is, its worth can be known only by the physician after observing the effects. Pulp which is like interpretative knowledge may be mistaken but the knowledge received by inspiration from God cannot be. When man gets into his second different life after performing austerities and receiving inspirational knowledge and seeing the hidden realities, he discards the concept of apparent cause and effect and considers God only to be the causer of the causes. He does not believe in the first cause which is what the philosophers believe. He does not have any opposition to the ultimate effect. He flies with the bride of truth and sincerity behind the curtain of the groups of the angels just as the sun flies in the horizons. Rather, even beyond the horizon and the heavens, which is beyond the space being an abode of souls and wisdom; and he himself becomes one of that world of no matter, no space, no time. You elderly with all knowledge may know that the wisdoms of all of us are only shadows and like shadows they fall in prostration on the feet of the perfect soul.

chapters.title: Clear, Semi-Clear and Direct Information
chapters.subtitle: Similitude of Nass (clearly expressed statements with Qiyas (Logical assessment)

paras: Mujtahid is the person who strives to show the right path; when aware of the direct, clear-cut statements in the Quran, he does not go after indirect and unclear statements. If he does not get clear-cut statements, he goes after nearest possible speculation to get the spirit of the whole matter. Nass or clear-cut statements may be considered as divine inspirations from the Divine spirit; and the logical-intelligence-based-assessment as Qiyas which is partial and subordinate to nass. Wisdom acquired its assessing capacity and honourable status from the soul and therefore, the soul cannot be subordinate to wisdom. Soul casts its impressions upon wisdom, and wisdom proceeds to make assessments. Therefore, there is no parity between soul and wisdom as wisdom does not contain those causes and citations that soul has. Sometimes, wisdom misunderstands the impacts of the soul as the soul itself. That is not correct. Its impacts are different from itself. The difference is like the one between the sun and its brightness. The sun’s brightness is far far away from its actuality. For example, if the soul puts its impressions upon you as it did with Noah, you will not ask as to where the ocean is, where is the ark and where is the deluge; and straight away go to build the ark as Noah did. Therefore, a person on the path of searching gets pleased temporarily with the sun’s brightness and through it, he tries to catch the sun itself.

sections.heading: Sun’s Light and Spiritual Light
paras: But this light is a lowly material light and is destructible. It is not permanent and comes and goes during days and nights. One who has penetrated into the source to real (spiritual) light and settled there, has gone into its depth and permanently remains there. Neither the clouds come in the way of this light nor does it set, and one has no reason to cry over its separation as it never separates: Such a person belongs to the upper most world like the heavens: and even and if he belongs to the lowest world of materials, upon getting the real light is changed into one of the upper world,

sections.heading: Four Sufi Divisions
paras: [According to one of the sufi ways of explanation of every thing of the world, is of any of these four types:

1) Nasoot, the lowest world of matter of which earth is a part along with all material things connected with it. Stars, planets, plants, animals and even the physical man and also the physical worshipful acts are nasoot.
2) The other is Jabaroot: the world of commands, grandeur, laws and dominance which controls all affairs of the lowest world of Nasoot through God’s powers of attributes.
3) The third is Malakoot: the world of angels making exceptions to laws, and of spirits and intangible substances and of the action-based names or actions of God.
4) Lahoot the world of the essence of God, which is the highest and above all.

Those who annihilate themselves in the love of God or Godliness also get elevated to this world. That is the meaning of Aulia Allah, friends of God, is that they are His friends in this world — Translator’s Note]

The one made of mud, the ordinary man belonging to the world of Nasoot, does not have the capacity to bear the light of the reality upon him for all times; just as the earth will burn and be incapable of generating any living being if the rays of sun fall upon continuingly. Similarly, fishes can live for the entire life in water, but snakes as amphibians cannot do so. That is why those with all the connection with the lowest material world of Nasoot cannot go to the level of Lahoot, the highest world of Lahoot. But there are many poisonous snakes in the hills that can bite the fishes. Similarly, there are many tricky fellows who project themselves as the men of Lahoot (pseudo sufis) and deceive the innocent people, but when they see the real sufis who are full like the ocean, they get frightened. There are many fish like (real) sufi’s in the world who swim in large oceans, who with their marvellous magical powers can convert the snakes into fishes. Go with these fishes if you are a snake so that you may swim like fishes in the ocean. They are the fishes of majesty in the ocean and their magic is a permissible magic.

They have converted many impossibilities into real incidents like an accursed fellow becoming a noble man. Poison becomes sugar at their hands and a stone becomes a precious gem. Dust has become gold; stones have become gems and feet have become heads. But those who reject them do not see them as anything but ordinary men. Even if I narrate the affairs of those great men till the doomsday, it will not end. Ney, even if a hundred doomsdays also pass.

chapters.title: Attention Need to Learn
chapters.subtitle: Discipline of the disciples and audiences while hearing the statements of wisdom and grace from the masters

sections.heading: Repetition Needed to Teach
paras: There are those who feel grieved upon my repeating certain matters, but repetition is like a second life for me, in my view. When the flame of the lamp is doubled, it becomes brighter. And by repeated impressions of the transformations dust becomes gold (as has happened in geological epochs). In the presence of a single disinterested fellow in a gathering of thousands of seekers of truth, the provider of information feels stopped. These passer of the message while revealing the secrets, demand such attention from the audience like Israfil who is in constant attention of the command of God to blow in the trumpet (saur), even though it comes out only once at the time of the ending of the world. But Israfil does not know that time and therefore waits in attention as if it may be given any time during his entire life.

They have pride and sense of superiority like the kings and expect service from the worldly men because they come from elevated place. So long as you do not show them due respect and attention, you cannot get any benefit from their teachings. They will not hand over the trust to you, unless you humble yourself to take it. Yet they will not care for every petty respect as what they say is from the court of the highest level. The respect you show to them should be in accordance with their status. They are not devoid of services that they would feel your services to be an obligation for them.

sections.heading: No Discouragement
paras: Inspite of people’s lack of taste of their consciousness, they scatter away the royal offerings before them. And do not prevent yourself from doing so, O rider of the heavens. Run your horse upon the heavens and do not look at these grieved, disinterested fellows. Great is that preacher, who without caring for opposition, jumps his horse to the other side of the moat full of fire. You should warm up your horse so much that it should strive for the heights of the heavens. The disinterested and jealous people might have shut their eyes. But do not care for them and set fire to the dryness and wetness of the disinterested and the fire of jealousy. If you feel shy of speaking of the secrets to the people, first of all set that shyness itself on fire. Shyness, of its own, does not come from the world of non-existence; it comes about only when it feels the heat of a bold man. All and sundry do not feel shy of any act. It is a quality only of the bold and brave, who feel the fear of failure resulting in shame.

chapters.title: Identify the Enemy for Proper Defence
chapters.subtitle: Every animal identifies its enemy by its odour and protects itself. Destruction and loss are of the one who is enemy of the one from whom there is no scope for refuge, escape and fight

paras: A horse recognises the smell and sound of a lion. It is very rare that it would not recognise, in spite of being an animal. Rather, every animal recognises its enemy by its marks and identity. The bat does not fly during daytime but comes out during night like a lonely thief. Of all the deprived ones, bat is the greatest that it is an open enemy of the sun. Neither can it fight it in the open field, nor it can cause pains to it through its hatred. Yet the sun out of its generosity and greatness does not tear it into pieces out of anger.

And it even does not hide its face from the bat out of the anger and wrath of the bat. It is its generosity and grace in the largest extent that it leaves it molested as otherwise, what harm a bat can do to the sun.

Therefore, if you have to have an enemy, have it in accordance with your status, so that you may be in a position to control him. If a drop becomes an enemy of the sea, it is nothing but foolishness and self-disgracing. Its designs do not go farther than his beard. How can it tear the throat and chest of the moon? The enmity of the common people for the saints is similar.

This was about the enemy of the sun. What about the saintly people who are the enemies of the sun’s enemy? O enemy of that sun before whose grandeur and greatness, other sun and stars tremble in fear! You are not its enemy but enemy of your own self. What care will fire have for you if you volunteer and become its fuel. It is impossible that with your getting burnt, they will get reduced, or they will feel sorry upon your pain and wrath.

sections.heading: God’s Kindness Is Different
paras: God’s kindness is not like the kindness of man. Man’s kindness for anyone is due to his sorrowful situation. It is a reaction to someone’s miserable condition. People’s concern for others is mixed up with wrath, but God’s concern has nothing to do with wrath and sorrow. The quality of His mercy cannot be compared with any as it is impossible to know His essence; As such you should take it only as a mark and hint for your lowly understanding.

chapters.title: Learning Through Models and Direct Learning
chapters.subtitle: Difference between the understanding on similitude basis and simple followership; and that upon its reality and contents

paras: The marks of the mercies of God are observable like fruits on a tree, but none else than He can know their reality. The realities of the qualities of that Perfect being cannot be understood other than through some markings and examples. Our wisdom is incapable of understanding it just as a child cannot understand the pleasures of cohabitation excepting by telling him of the taste of sweets. He does not know what cohabitation with a woman is and its pleasure can be told to be like sweet like sugar. These pleasures are entirely different and incomparable. There can never be a comparison between these pleasures. But a wise man has attributed the two as the sources of pleasure to tell the child that they are similar, so that the child may understand through an example. Therefore, if you say about some matters that you have understood, it is not correct; if you even say that you have not understood, that is also not fully fully wrong. With all this it is clear that some kind of knowledge is known, but not all.

sections.heading: Opposing Views of Study
paras: Some one may ask you whether you know Noah, the prophet of God and the light of the soul. And you say: How can I remain without knowing him? He is more well known than the sun and moon. All children in their schools and the imams in the masjids, clearly read his name in the Quran and clearly explain the incidents of his life”. What you say is true, as you know him through the attributes about him, even though you may not know his reality.

And if you say: “How can I know about Noah, who was a chosen worshiper of God and a holy spirit. What am I and what is my capacity to understand him? Only one who is like him can understand him. I am a lame ant. How can I know about the elephant? How can a mosquito know about H. Israfil?”

This statement of yours is also correct, because you do not know him as per his real capacity. The incapacity to understand the realities is a weakness of the common people. But you should not remain at this level, as the perfect ones know the secrets of the secrets, which are clearly visible to their eyes. God’s existence and the secrets of His essence are the farthest of the things to be known by our knowing power and insight. But these do not remain hidden from His secret bearers. When God Himself is known to them who else is there whose essence and qualities remain hidden from them? They know about everything in the whole universe.

sections.heading: Wisdom Alone Cannot Solve Problems
paras: Wisdom based on deductive analysis says that all this is impossible to know. One should not believe in anything without logical analysis and corroborating evidence; but a Qutub, who is a great leader around whom everything moves as on an axis, says: “You are a slow mover. You consider that thing to be impossible which is beyond your grasping capacity. Do you not know that some incidents have become clear to you now, which were not clear earlier? [Many things were unclear earlier like the static condition of earth, and changes occur because of the motion of the heaven; but now it is well known that earth is not static but is in motion — Translator]. When God has released you from the prison of the senses, do not make the field of Tiya as your prison in which Bani Israil roamed about for forty years, without getting out of it.

When you got rid of hundreds of troubles of poverty, be sure that you will be rid of the troubles of sorrows and pains of ignorance. Consider this also to be easy for you that it will provide ease for you to know unrevealed secrets; (through meditation) as otherwise due to your lacking hope, sweetness of love will turn into bitterness of melancholy. O, Rumi, father of goodness, stop further discourse in this matter, as it has no end. If you want to speak of the positive and negative aspects of things, be clear in explaining matters.

chapters.title: Relativity and Dimension Change Matters
chapters.subtitle: Addition and subtraction between the negative and positive aspects of matters in a single thing due the difference between dimension and relativity

paras: Denial and approval of a single thing are correct, because these are from two different points of view and two different relations. The statement: “You did not throw when you did throw” is in relation to each other, negative and positive, and both are correct. This is related to the incident of the Prophet’s throwing a handful of dust toward the enemies during the battle of Badr as a result of which they were blinded for sometime resulting in their defeat. This incident is referred to as: “You did not throw when you threw but Allah threw:” wa maa ramayta iz ramayta, walaak in allaha ramaa: (Anfaal 8: 17).

He said: You threw, because this act was done by you and you did not throw, because the power to do that act was given by God. There is a limit to the power of man. A handful of dust cannot be a cause for the defeat of an army. The hand is yours, but the act of throwing is ours. With this relativity both the statement of negation and approval are correct. Prophets are well recognised by their opponents just as they recognise their own children, with the help of many symbols and arguments. But with jealousy and envy they hide this and plead by saying that they do not know. When God said in another place that ‘He recognises’ and at another place He said: No one recognises them other than Me”: and He also said: They are hidden under my garment, which is not known to anyone else than Me.” You may understand this in clear terms that it is due to relativity, just as you know Noah and also do not know him (as explained under proceeding part). Such negation and approval is shown in many statements, which are relative to persons, situations and incidents. The matter relating to the everlasting life and anhilation of the aulia has to be understood similarly. Such things have come in many Hadith(s) which are as per the differences of persons, places and times.

chapters.title: Meaning of Fanaa and Baqaa
chapters.subtitle: Problems of Fanaa (anhilation) and Baqaa (everlasting life) of the perfect Darvesh

paras: Someone said that there is no darvesh in the world; and if there is one, he is not a darvesh. That darvesh who is not there from the point of his life as his essence, as his qualities have submerged into God’s and is lost to himself. This is just like a lamp in front of the sun, which has no existence in comparison with sun’s light; but from the point of view of accounting, it exists, because if you keep cotton upon it, it catches fire and burns. The lamp only becomes deficient and does not give you light as the sun has destroyed its light.

If you put one kilogram of vinegar in one hundred kilograms of honey and it is dissolved; and if you taste the mixture, there is no taste of vinegar. But if you weigh it, it is heavy by one kilogram. Similarly, a deer fell down unconscious before a lion, it lost its existence within its own existence.

This kind of assessment of the imperfect people is not due to their not honouring of the works of God, but due to their excessive love for Him. The lover’s pulse beats with the love of God and keeps itself in the balance pan along with God. This does not mean that the lover claims parity with God. There is always a relationship between the lover and the beloved; yet there is a difference between the possible and inevitable. Such a lover of God by making such claim is very disrespectful to God from one angle. But, in fact, he has such great respect for Him, which is very rare.

sections.heading: Mixing of Opposites
paras: His being respectful and disrespectful at the same time is the mixing of opposites and appears to be absurd. If the respectfulness is toward his own essence, it is disrespect; and if it is toward the essence of God, it is respect. If you look at him in his apparent condition, he is disrespectful as he claims parity with God. His claim of Love for Him is nothing other than parity. But, if you go deep into him, you will see that there is no such acclaim at all. His existence is annihilated before the Great King.

If you consider a sentence: ‘X died’, though grammatically X is a subject, but it has not done any act that the subject does. But in fact, he is an object, as he is a victim of death which is the actual subject. How can he be a subject to do an act when he is so impacted that all activity has gone away from him?

chapters.title: Impacts of Separation
chapters.subtitle: Story of a trustee of Sadar Jahan who was accused of crime and he ran away out of fear from Bukhara; and then his love brought him back to the process of law. Dying for the beloved is easy for the lovers

paras: A slave of Sadar Jahan of Bukhara was victim of a criminal charge and absconded to avoid punishment. For about ten years he roamed about here and there. Sometimes in Khorasan, and in Kohistan and in forests. After ten years, as a result of his enthusiasm of love, he got disgusted of separation and helplessness. He said to himself: “I cannot bear separation any longer. I cannot become free of the fear of the pangs of separation and bear it anymore.

sections.heading: Impacts of Separation
paras: With separation from water, earth becomes dry and infertile, and water becomes yellow, dirty and shallow due to stagnation and lack of movement. So also life-giving air without blowing becomes polluted and contagious. Fuel becomes ash and gets scattered with separation from spring season, garden becomes as house of sicknesses and the leaves of its trees become yellow and fall down. Separation from the sharp wisdom of friends, thoughts and sensibilities becomes like an archer with a broken bow. The hell, with separation from the graces of God has become burning fire; and the plant of rattan with separation from strength has become thin and wavery. If I go on telling you about the effects of separation, I shall have to tell till the doomsday about the sparks of separation and it will be just like one out of a hundreds thousand. Therefore, do not go too much after knowing about the pangs of separation. But only be saying: “O God, save me and protect me.”

Everything that is pleasing in this world ultimately gets separated. Therefore, think of the moments of its separation. Many have already been pleased earlier of what is pleasing you now; and finally, it went away from them and got mixed up in air and flew away from them. It will run away from you also and therefore do not get infatuated with it. Run away from it well before, it runs away from you. Well before the loss of your things say what H. Maryam said to her nafs (self): “I want the protection of God from you”.

chapters.title: Fears Lead to Victories
chapters.subtitle: Appearance of the Holy spirit in the form of man when H. Maryam was bathing and H. Maryam’s seeking the protection of God

sections.heading: Extraordinary Impacts of Jibra’iil
paras: H. Maryam saw a soul inspiring very beautiful person in her privacy, which suddenly came about from the earth. Gabriel was, bright like sun and moon. He was very handsome; without any veil and came about just as the sun rises in the east. H. Maryam’s limbs started shivering out of fright as she was without clothings. Jibra’iil was so beautiful that if Yusuf were to look at him, he would have peeled his fingers just as the women of Egypt pealed their fingers upon looking at him. Like flowers he came about from mud, just as thoughts come about from the heart. H. Maryam lost her self-control and said that she would go into the protection of God. She said Inni a’uzu bil Rahman minka in kunta taqiyya. I seek refuge from you with God most gracious: do not come near, if you fear God; (Maryam: 19: 18). That clean one Maryam was in the habit of turning toward the unseen (God) whenever in distress. She had understood the world as an unsettled place and she had made God’s court as a fort for her defence, so that it may be a fort till the end of her life so as to disable the Satan from crossing over it. She had not seen a stronger fort than the refuge of God. She had made her residence near that fort.

When she looked at Jibra’iil’s mind spelling styles, which would injure a man’s heart before whom kings and the armies had fallen. The emperors of wisdom have fallen unconscious. Hundreds of thousands of kings have become his slaves. Hundreds of thousands bright full moons had lost their brightness. Venus did not have the strength to face him. Even a man with perfectness of wisdom would forget all his engagements.

sections.heading: God’s Beauty Through Jibra’iil
paras: What can I say about the beauty of the Lord, when His angel is so beautiful? His beauty has pierced itself into my chest and my throat has felt the charm of His beauty and dried and I cannot say more about Him. I can call myself as the smoke of His fire. And many others claim to have seen many of His symbols, but all those are not worthy of consideration. I am only an evidence of the impacts of His impressions. There is no need to prove the existence of sun. That itself is its evidence through its light. Shadow cannot be an evidence of its existence; the most that can be said is that shadow is dependent upon it. When there is no sun there is no shadow. His greatness is such that, not only that it is itself an evidence of itself and it is in front of all realisations and the rest just follow them. All realisations ride upon lame donkeys, but in vehicles are flying like arrows on the fast-flying air. If He goes away from anyone none can catch him and if others run away from Him, He can catch and stop them. He is very close to man. Yet understanding about Him is far far away. Many have understood Him, but they are not satisfied, and they are in more and more searching. One thought flies like the falcon and other tears things like a shot out arrow. One’s thinking is slow like a ship with sails and another is still in confusion.

sections.heading: Difficulties in Knowing God
paras: When there is a symptom from God all the people go toward it like the hunters that go after a prey; and when the symptom disappears, they get disappointed and like owls go into the ruins. A keen hunter keeps one eye closed and another open so as to concentrate on the prey with all attention through the open eye so that the prey is visible to him accurately. And when the prey goes away very far, he gets confused and says whether it was really a pray or was it an illusion. This is the situation in respect of those who try to understand God.

sections.heading: Nights, Constriction and Autumns Are Needed
paras: In such situations wisdom lies in taking rest for some time so as to provide rest and strength to the seekers. This rest is necessary as otherwise by constant thinking and working one would get exhausted. Had there been no darkness of night, all the people in their greed would burn up themselves by nonstop working. Everybody would set fire to himself because of his greed and desire to earn more. Night comes like a treasure of mercy, so that people may be rid of their greed for some time. Similarly, a person spiritually marching on the path of God gets tired and constriction of heart starts which is for his own good and to avoid disappointment. You are engaged in expending your potentialities in both constriction and expansion of heart; and in order to expand, there has to be a supply of needs from the accumulated treasure of energy which comes about in constriction. Had there been a summer throughout, the sun’s heat would have set the garden on fire and burnt the roots of the seedlings in such way that it would never become green and fresh anymore. If the autumn is sour, it is also benevolent. Summer burns as well as smiles and gives the same to others.

sections.heading: Seek Food of Wisdom
paras: Observe expansion in constriction, when it occurs upon you and face it with afresh, without wrinkles on your forehead. While children are happy in green fields, the elders feel that the heart is for tasting sorrows, and lungs are for laughter. Children’s views are upon green grass for pleasure like the donkey’s but the wise think of the ultimate results of actions. Like the donkeys a child considers grass as pleasurable, but the wiseman thinks of the accounts of the next life. Food is like the grass that is provided by the butcher to the sheep, which is bitter as it is given to provide fresh tasty meat to us. You should be careful to eat the grass of wisdom as it is given free to you by God, and it is a great grant. You have misunderstood the meaning of God’s saying: kulu min rizqihi: enjoy the sustenance which He furnishes: (Mulk: 67: 15) as referring to food and not as to wisdom. The sustenance of wisdom is much better in grade, as it will not catch your neck in the end.

sections.heading: Food for Body, Food for Soul
paras: If you shut your mouth for food for body, another mouth will open in you which will swallow the morsels of the secrets of nature. If you deprive your devil of this body of the milk of physical nourishment, this will result in the grant of great gifts which are far better than milk just as a baby after giving up milk, gets varieties of delicious dishes. The grants that you get are in the grants of wisdom and gnosis. I have just given a little heat to improve upon this subject, but it is only half-cooked. You may hear everything from Hakeem Sanai’s “Ilaahi Nama”, who is a great knower of the secrets of nature and an honour for all gnostics: “swallow pains of heart and the bread of those who increase pain through sweets, as a wise man swallows pains of wisdom, learning and research, as against a child which eats sweets.”

sections.heading: Achievement After Great Struggle
paras: Sweet sugar gives good taste, but it is a fruit of the garden of sorrows. The pleasure given by it is an injury; and pain is a soothing balm for it. Hold on to sorrows close to your body and heart with all love, and then you will know what pleasure is. One who cannot see the beauty of the Syrian city of Damascus should stand on the nearby hillock of Rabwa, from where he can see the entire city of Damascus and its beauty. A wiseman sees wine in grapes which is the end product of grapevine. So also, a lover sees everything of the beloved when the beloved is far off (and less when nearby). Yesterday I saw coolies quarrelling with each other to carry a heavy load each one telling the others that he has the lion’s strength to lift it. They had seen great benefit in carrying this load, and therefore, trying to snatch from the others. This, they were doing in the hope of getting the wages for this job.

Where are the wages for this labour, which are pittance given by a poor person? Try to lift the loads provided by God. He will give you a treasure for this job. That will be a treasure which will be of use to you when you sleep under a load of sand of your grave. This treasure is your own earned and not what you inherit. This wealth will walk in front of your funeral and accompany you on your journey to the other world and be your co-traveller in grave. You may die now itself in order to be with the everlasting love on the date of death.

sections.heading: Patience in Constriction and Expansion
paras: Patience looks at beautiful rosy faces and tufts from behind the curtain of hard struggle which sees pains as mirrors, in which, it sees the opposite face of joys. After the opposite faces, it sees wide expanses, grandeur and majesty all around. Consider these two situations of expanse and constriction as the opening and closing of the palm; it may be open and flat or close like the fist. When it is open it is wide and loses it loses it holdings and when close it holds. When open it expands and gives and when close it collects and stores. It should not be always open or close and change according to circumstances just as the wings of the birds which open and close one after another to maintain their flight. Both opening and closing are equally important and necessary. Similarly, is case of the constriction and expansion of the soul, which should be together like the two wings of birds.

chapters.title: Initial Shocks of Jibra’iil
chapters.subtitle: Jibra’iil’s telling Maryam not to fear as “I am the Messenger of God. Do not be anxious and do not hide from me”

sections.heading: Jibra’iil Initially Frightens
paras: Maryam was shocked for a moment and got perturbed just like the fish out of water. Jibra’iil who was like the grace of God called her and said: “I am the trustee of my Lord, do not run away from me. I am the honourable one of God. Do not turn your face from me. Do not be disturbed by such carriers of the secrets.”

While he was telling this and clean light was emanating from his lips going up to the highest stars. And he continued: Why do you run away from my state. I am the king and flag bearer of the next world. My home and its materials are there in the next world of non-materials (spiritual). I am having this physical personality before you for a short time. O Maryam. Look at me. I am in a troublesome body; I am a physical body like the moon, and I am also a thought within the heart.

sections.heading: Jibra’iil the Most Welcome
paras: “Thought, when it comes into your heart, settles down. It is with you, wherever you go. But there is a timely thought also which is like the false dawn, which comes and goes momentarily. But I am like the true dawn and from the light of God, which remains for the whole day which lasts, and it never ends at night. O daughter of Imran. Do not recite the phrase la howl (strength is only with God) at me which is recited to chase away evil forces as I have come from la howl himself. My base and sustenance is la howl only, the light of which is prior to it. You are seeking the refuge of God against me; but from the very beginning itself, I am the written down fact of His refuge. I am that refuge which is the place of your deliverance. You recite “A’uzu” (I seek refuge) and seek the same thing; and I myself am the refuge.

sections.heading: Non-Recognition of God
paras: “There is no more troublesome thing than non-recognition. You are very much with the loved one, but you are not aware of love. You consider a friend as a stranger. You consider a matter of pleasure as tragedy. God, as our friend is showing so many benevolences, but like an insincere fellow you are running away from Him. He has given us a date palm which is helping to us in so many ways, but like thiefs we consider it as a scaffold. Such musky fragrance He has provided to us like the fragrant tufts, but with our foolishness, we consider the tufts as shackles. With such great concern for us He has flowed the river Nile for us, but as we are Pharaohs, its water has become blood for us. This blood tells us: “No I am not blood but water, and do not waste me by flowing me down”. It also says: “I am Yusuf; but you quarrelsome fellow consider me as a wolf. You do not see that a dignified friend becomes an enemy like the snake if you go on opposing him, in spite of the fact that his flesh and fat is the same as it was. It is not he, but his temperament that has changed.”

chapters.title: Love of the Country of Origin
chapters.subtitle: That lawyer’s determination to go to Bukhara without taking due care

paras: Leave the lamp of Maryam burning, as that heart-burnt-lawyer is going toward Bukhara from where he had run away. He was greatly impatient and within a furnace and was telling: turn your face and run toward Sadar Jahan. Bukhara is an origin of intellectualism and learning, and whoever is an intellectual is a Bukharite. The heart of your master also is a Bukhari (intellectual) in this sense, and while sitting before him, do sit down with all respect as otherwise you will be put to great disgrace. Only with humility you can enter into the heart of your master, as otherwise the tidal movement and its rise and fall will cause difficulties in his teaching. He is a fortunate fellow whose nafs (self) has humbled itself and become obedient; and he is like a dead one who is kicked by his self-pride.

sections.heading: Return of the Separated Lover
paras: Separation from Sadar Jahan had dominated his mind and torn off his limbs into pieces. He told to himself: “I shall get up and go back to the place. I shall not think of any other way as I am not like an infidel to my beloved. I shall go back and fall down before the beloved who, I am sure, always thinks well of me. I shall tell him: “I have dropped down my life before you. You may give life, or you may slaughter me, as a goat is slaughtered. O my moon, dying and getting killed before you is better than becoming a king of people in any other place. I have tested this thousands of times that I cannot consider my life to be worth living without you. O my loving heart, sing again the song for my regaining life. Sit down my camel, so that I may sit upon you to go toward my beloved. O earth, swallow my tears of separation which are enough to satisfy your thirst. O my life, be satisfied with the clean friendship that I shall have shortly. Great is my situation that my lost happy occasion is coming back to me. O sweet wind, I thank you. You have brought for me the fine fragrance and spread it all around.”

He also said: “Goodbye my friend, I am on my way to my commander and receiver of services. I am burning in the passion of love every moment. I am determined to go whatever may be the result. Though my beloved has made his heart hard as granite, but my life has determined to go to Bukhara. That is the city of my friend and of my ruler. Love of the place where the beloved resides is patriotism in the lover’s view.

chapters.title: Best Place Is Where the Beloved Resides
chapters.subtitle: A beloveds question to the lover as to which city is the best, most populous, most prosperous and most lovely and the answer of the lover

paras: A beloved told her lover: “O young man, you cave seen many cities. Tell me which is the best city that you have seen?” He said: “That city is the best where the beloved resides. The place where the beloved encamps even if it is in a forest, or in a place as narrow as the eyelet of the needle. Every place where the moonlike Yusuf resides, whether it is paradise or the depth of the well. With you my life provider, even the hell is a heaven and even a prison is a green garden. The hell is an agreeable and gracious place if you are with me. And without you, sweet smelling plants and flowers are like lumps of fire of the hell. I shall be happy wherever you are with me, even if it is a grave. That place is better than both the material and spiritual worlds, where you think of me.
Let me pass on from this as the lover of Sadar Jahan is getting impatient due to my ignoring the affairs of his beloved.

chapters.title: Fate Drags to End
chapters.subtitle: Preventing by his friends from going to Bukhara and his refusal to heed

paras: A friend advised him: “You ignorant fellow, think of the consequences if you have any wisdom. Look at your front and back with your wisdom, and do not burn yourself like the moth. Are you mad that you think of going to Bukhara and consider yourself to be fit to get into chains and prison? Your enemy is biting pieces of iron with his teeth out of his anger for you and searching for you with twenty eyes. He is sharpening his dagger for you. He is like a famished dog and you are a morsel of food. You have been protected so far, and God has helped you, and you are going toward the prison. Even if ten different types of soldiers come in disguise in search of you, your wisdom ought to avoid them. But when there is none appointed to catch you here, you are tying yourself from both front and back side”.

sections.heading: Hidden Soldiers Drag Men to Fate
paras: His friend was not looking at that hidden soldier, which was his in-depth hidden love, which had imprisoned him. There is a hidden soldier to watch a soldier who compels the soldier to behave like watchful dog. The anger of the king of love had caught his heart and handed over to the soldiery and disgrace. They torture him and he cannot escape. May God save me from such hidden soldiers.

Whenever you see someone going alone toward his own destruction, think that he is not lonely. He is going under a watchful (hidden) soldier. If he is aware of this soldier, he would have complained to the King of kings. But he is not aware of him. He would have bowed down before that King in so much grief that the frightening devil would have been compelled to grant him peace. But he does not do so.

sections.heading: Wrong Self-Assessment
paras: You are less worthy than an ant, but you consider yourself as great and out of this illusory greatness you are blindfolded, and you do not see the hidden soldier appointed to drag you to your fate. You have become arrogant because of your self-made wings and feathers of your false achievements which are dragging you toward disaster. You have got light feathers and desire to go high above when these feathers get polluted by dust, become heavy and fell you down. Be careful and try not to get the feathers polluted by dust. But your ears have gone deaf and my advice to you is considered as ancient wisdom.
Anyway, his friends advised the lover very much, but it was of no use as he was determined to put himself in fire.

chapters.title: Lovers Only Know of Love
chapters.subtitle: Reply of the lover to his advisers and warners

sections.heading: Lovers Have Many Lives
paras: He told his adviser: “Stop, no more advice is required. The thought that has caught hold of me is very strong. your advice has further strengthened me. You do not know what love is. Even stalwarts like Imam Abu Hanifa and Imam Shafei have not given any instruction in the matter of love. Yet you have dared to advise and thereby caused greater pain to me. Do not frighten me of getting killed as I am myself thirsty of my own blood. Lovers face new death every moment and every death is of a different kind. [For example: Lovers of God die a red death when they kill their passions; green death when they discard the world and get into poverty; black death, which they get when troubled by the people. That is why they believe in the death, well before death. These are spiritual deaths, and the final death is only physical — Qazi Sajjad Hussain]. Lovers have two hundred lives with a grand light and every moment they sacrifice these lives. By sacrificing one life they get ten lives in recompense. That is, ten times, which you may see in the Quran: man jaa’a bi alhasanati falahu ashru amsalaha: He who does good shall have ten times as much to his credit: (Al an’aam: 6: 160)

sections.heading: Lovers Do Not Fear Death
paras: If my beloved’s face sheds my blood, I shall dance and sacrifice my life at it. I have got this experience that my death itself is my life. If I get rid of this physical life, I am sure to get an eternal life. O my advisers: kill me, do kill me. There is life within life for me only in my getting killed. O my brightening face, O the life of my life, give me your company by absorbing my soul into yourself. I have a beloved which sets fire to my interior. If it wants to trample my eyes, let it trample. (the verses containing the points in this paragraph are in Arabic).

I expressed some feelings in Arabic, and you ask me to speak in Persian, though Arabic is much sweeter than Persian. But you should know the love has hundreds of other languages. When the fragrance of the beloved blooms, all the languages get wonderstruck and feel their inabilities.
Now, I stop at this as the beloved has started talking; and cast your full attention. God alone knows the entire truth.

But do not believe this stopping of the lover’s talk about the beloved. He is treacherous and breaks his promise. Even from the gallows, he will start talking about love. This lover’s going to Bukhara is not for learning as others do. His beloved’s beauty is his teacher, and he learns from the beloved’s face which is like a book for him. He is silently reading the face, but the role of his learning by heart is reaching the empyrean and the throne of his beloved. His learning is his silent rote, silent enthusiasm and silent dance; and it is not from the great well-known book — Ziarat, of Imam Muhammad, its chapters and the book — Silsila (literally meaning chain).

sections.heading: Bukhara: a Great Centre for Learning
paras: The chains of the lovers are the curly, musk spilling fragrance of the beloveds and the repetition of lessons is the repeated continuation of the lesson on the beloveds face. Do not go into the juristic problem whether one who had given in trust a bag containing coins to another without counting before delivery, can complain of deficiency upon return. Tell such a questioner that the treasure of God cannot be filled in bags. Do not enter into discussions of legal questions like Khula, where a women seeks divorce from husband, and mubara’at where both husband and wife mutually seek divorce, which are all discussed in Bukhara.

Discussion on any matter creates a particular mood as quality of particular thing has its own meaning and impact. You have occasions to learn many skills in Bukhara, and you can achieve them only when you seek them in humiliation.

sections.heading: No Language Can Express Love
paras: But this visitor to Bukhara was not for learning. His insight was looking for a light, brighter than the sun. One who finds out the path of insight in seclusion does not go in search of expertise in apparent learnings of matters. He finds meanings even in meaningless sounds as some saints got into ecstasy upon hearing the sound of the churning of the water wheel. He does not go after certainty of knowledge (ilmal yaqin) but after certainty of sight (ainal yaqin) as stated about the difference in the Quran: (Takasur: 102: 5 and 7). He shares his drinks with the beauty of the soul. He develops contempt for hearsay knowledge but relies upon actual seeing of the interior spirit of things.

Seeing with the eyes dominates over wisdom and it is for this reason that people are overlapped with the affairs of the apparent material world, taking it only as real; and the affairs of the other spiritual world as hearsay.
Now, let us go to the affairs of that young lover as he is getting forlorn in his love for Sadar Jahan.

chapters.title: Impacts of Beloved’s Place
chapters.subtitle: Turning of that lover’s face toward Bukhara

paras: That blood shedding lover turned toward Bukhara with a burning heart and marched fast. The sand of the desert was like silk for him and the water of the large river, Jaihoon was a small pool for him. Forests were like gardens for him, and he was like a happy flower picker. He passed through Samarqand, a place called as sugary, but he was not interested in its sweetness, but his entire faith was in Bukhara. O Bukhara, you were the one to increase intellect, but you have snatched my wisdom and faith. I am in the search of the full bright moon. I have become thin like a crescent; and I am searching for the highly placed Sadar in the place where shoes and sandals are kept.

sections.heading: Impact of Beloved’s Place
paras: When he reached nearby to Bukhara and looked at its suburbs, he found a brightness coming out of the blackness of his sorrows. He fell down flat for some time without consciousness as his wisdom flew into the garden of mysteries. People sprinkled rose water upon his face thinking of this unconsciousness as mental and physical. They were not aware of the rose water that gives back consciousness to the lover. He had seen a hidden garden and the disasters caused by love had separated him from himself.

You are frigid. You cannot understand these things. Though you are like sugarcane, but you are not aware of the fact that sugar comes out of sugarcane. You are wise enough and you have the materials of wisdom, but you are not aware of many things that you have not seen, as God said: wa anzala junudan lam tarawha: and sent down forces which you did not see: (Tawba: 9: 26).
All this talk has no end. Let us go fast so that, the youth may go to Bukhara.

chapters.title: Warning to Avoid Risks
chapters.subtitle: Entry of the lover into Bukhara and his friends warning him to hide himself

paras: He happily entered into Bukhara, the city of his beloved and the city of peace, like the bird that flies high in the sky, which is embraced by the moon telling it also, to embrace it. Whoever looked at him told him: “Go away from Bukhara before you are found out. Do not sit anywhere here and run away fast, because the wrathful king has been in search of you from the past ten years. For God’s sake, do not go after your own blood and do not rely upon your magic spells and life-giving breaths. You had been the top police officer of Sadar Jahan. You were wise, his confident and chief engineer. You were his consultant and were very honourable before him. But you got accused of a crime. You deceived him and ran away out of the fear of punishment. You were saved from punishment. Now, why do you get yourself caught. You had resorted to a hundred designs and escaped from troubles. Either your foolishness or your death has brought you back here. Your wisdom was such as to talk critically about planet Mercury. But you should know that death makes a fool of wisdom and the wise. You are that rabbit which is searching for the lion. What has happened to your intelligence, wisdom and wit? Death has hundreds of means to catch its victim. There is a saying that when death comes, the atmosphere shrinks. There are hundreds of ways of escape on the right and left, which get closed by death even for a strong python.”

sections.heading: Reply of the Lover to Advisers and Warners
paras: He said: “I suffer from the sickness of thirst and water drags me, and I go to it knowing fully well that water will kill me. No man suffering from chronic thirst will run away from water, even if it weakens and tires him for two hundred times. Though excessive water may swell my belly and my hands, the craze for water will not end. If I am asked about my inside, I would say; how good it would be if an ocean flows within me. Tell the goatskin of my stomach to burst, out of the force of water; and if I thus die, it will be a very clean death. Whereever I see a stream I desire that I should have been in its place. My hand and belly are swollen. My hand is like a tambourine and belly like a drum; and I beat the drum of my love for water like the flower, which survives upon water. If my beloved sheds my blood, I shall drink it sip by sip like the earth. The earth drinks blood and so also the baby in the womb; and I also do like them ever since I fell in love.

sections.heading: Lovers Do Not Fear Death and Pains
paras: During the night I boil over as a large vessel and drink (absorb) blood like sand from morning to night. I feel ashamed that I cheated Sadar Jahan by running away and avoided his anger and objects. Tell him to spill his anger on my inebriated life. He is the feast of sacrifice and the lover is a buffalo to be sacrificed. Whether a cow sleeps or eats, it is reared for sacrifice on the feast of sacrifice. Consider me as the cow of Musa which gave life to the dead. Let me be sacrificed and every part of my body be a cause of life to everyone in love. [Musa’s cow is referred to the incident in which Musa was ordered by God to sacrifice a cow and hit a piece of its flesh on a murdered person. Upon hitting, he regained life and told the name of the person who had murdered him: as referred to in the Quran: faqulna adribuhu biba’diha: So, we said: strike the body with a piece of the (heifer): (Baqara: 2: 73). The Musa’s cow was a sacrificed one, and an ordinary piece of its flesh was a life giver to the murdered person. By receiving a blow from the piece of flesh the dead man came back to life and that was due to God’s command: “strike it with a piece of flesh”.

sections.heading: Evolution from Mineral to Man and Angel
paras: “O honourable people! Sacrifice me as that cow with your spiritual exertions, if you want to see those invisible souls. Souls may assume visible, sensible, material bodies to be seen by your eyes. I died from the world of minerals and entered into a new life of plants. And when I died as a plant, and eaten by animals, I got a new animal life. And when I died as an animal, being eaten by man, I got new life of a man. Why should I then fear death. I was never annihilated. In the next occasion I shall be deprived of manness upon death, so that I may develop feathers and wings, and become an angel. And from this level of angel also I have to dive into the stream, as excepting the essence of God every thing is destructible as stated in Quran: kullu shaiin haalkun illa wajhahu: Everything that exists shall perish except God’s own face (Qasas: 28: 88). After this I shall be sacrificed from the status of the angel and become that which cannot be assessed by wisdom. Then, I shall become non-existent like the tunes of the organ which will tell: inna lillaahi wa inna ilaihi raajiun: to God we belong and to Him is our return (Baqara: 2: 156).

sections.heading: Live and Die for Love
paras: “Understand well about death, as everyone agrees that the water of life (Aab-e- Hayat) is hidden in darkness. (Grow on the borders of water bodies like the lotus, which like the man suffering from the disease of chronic thirst always remains with water. Its death is in water and it always lives with water and continuously drinks, and God alone knows best.

“O sorrowful lover, rigid and wet like the bedding soaked in water, you run away from the beloved out of the fear of life! You are a cause of disgrace for love! Look at the hundreds and thousands of people clapping in pleasure by looking at the sword of love! When you look at a stream pour down the water from your vessel into its water. Water never hesitates to mingle with water. When the water from the vessels gets mixed up with water, it gets lost in it and becomes one like it. By getting lost in water, it assumes the quality of immortality and thereafter neither it gets reduced in quantity nor it changes its shape. Your love for God should also be like this. Get lost in God and become immortal.”

chapters.title: Atlast Before the Beloved
chapters.subtitle: Lover’s approach to the beloved with lost hopes

paras: He continued to say: “I have hanged myself on a date palm as a matter of regret that I had gone away.”

He prostrated with his head and face on the dust like a rolling ball, with eyes full of tears, to go to Sadar Jahan. And washed his pale face with tears with the shroud and sword in his sand, as he was completely devoted and ready for any kind of punishment.

All the people around him waited to hear that he would be burnt or hanged. Sadar Jahan will give such a punishment to this fool, which has not been given to any unfortunate fellow till then. Like a moth he has considered the sparks of fire a lights, fallen like an idiot and lost life.

But they did not know that the lamp of love is not like other lamps. It is always bright, brighter and brightest. Its fire is quite different from the fire of other lamps. It appears as fire, but in fact, it is extreme pleasure.

chapters.title: The Deadly Mosque
chapters.subtitle: Narration of a mosque which killed its guests and of careless guest searching for death

paras: Hear this narration of a noble man of a mosque in the suburbs of Rey, the city from where came about the great Imam Fakhruddin Razi. Nobody used to sleep in this mosque during night with the fear that his children may not become orphans. Whoever that slept in it like a blind, careless fellow, went into the grave at dawn like the stars that also vanish from the sky. One should learn a lesson from this and become aware of the fact that the dawn of the doomsday is also about to come, and one should get up from sleep.

Everyone in the town used to say that there are ill-tempered fairies in the mosque who would kill anyone sleeping in it with a blunt sword. Some others would say that there was some magic spell which waited for somebody to arrive in it, with its enmity for human body and soul. Someone asked that a board should be hanged on the mosque warning strangers not to sleep in it if they wanted to protect their life, as death was waiting to catch them. One more fellow would say that it should be locked so that any unknowing fellow may not enter into it.

chapters.title: Bold Become Adventurers
chapters.subtitle: Coming of a guest into the mosque

sections.heading: Worth of Soul and Worthlessness of Body
paras: One night a guest came who had heard about the strange things of the mosque. He wanted to test the veracity of the matter as he was a brave and adventurous fellow. He believed that his head and body were of no worth; and if a small coin gets lost from the treasury, it is not a cause of worry. After all, what is the worth of a single man’s life or death. Tell the body to get lost, as it is only a model of no worth. Real worth is of the soul that is in it. Because God has blown His soul with grace within man as God has said in the Quran: fa iza sawwaituhu wa nafakhtu fihi min ruhi: when I have fashioned him (man) (in due proportion) and breathed into him My Spirit (Al Hijr: 15: 29 and also in Swad: 38: 72). Therefore, even if the body is annihilated, the soul remains intact. I shall be more graceful that I shall continue to exist as pure soul without the burden of the body, like the blow of air in the lute, which is different from the flute. And at the time of the sound of the trumpet (sur) of Israfil comes, my soul will get associated with the body like the union of the blow of air within the flute. I do not want to keep the blow of God’s wind away from me, until I become free like a pearl and shine and become precious, after getting out of the prison of oyster. God has also addressed to Jews to desire for death to give evidence of their truthfulness as stated in the Quran: if the abode of the hereafter in the providence of Allah is indeed for you alone and not to others of mankind (as you pretend), then long for death if you are truthful: Fatamanna ul mowta in kuntum saadiqin (Baqara: 2: 94). Longing for death is a proof of the claim. I am a truthful fellow; and therefore, I long for death.

chapters.title: People’s Sincere Advice
chapters.subtitle: Condemnation by the people of the loveful guest; their preventing and warning to avoid sleeping

paras: The people again warned him, not to sleep, so that his life taker may not crush him like seeds and said: “You insist so much because you are a stranger and unaware of the facts that whoever slept here was put to decline. This has not happened as an accident. It has happened many times which has been seen by all wisemen. Whoever that made this mosque as a residence for him for one night, has met with a murderous midnight. We have seen this not once, but five hundred times. What we say is out of experience and not by mere hearsay. The noble Prophet has said: Al dinu nasihatan: Religion is well wishing and sincerity. The opposite of sincerity in dictionary is selfishness. In giving advice, there is friendship and truthfulness, but in selfishness there is cheating and doggishness. What advice we give is purely out of our sincerity and well wishing. Therefore, do not turn away from wisdom.

chapters.title: Pleasures of Pain
chapters.subtitle: Reply of the lover to the advisers and condemners

paras: The Stanger said: “O my advisers, without any hesitation, I say that I am fully satisfied with the pleasures of this world. I am a searcher of injuries and I get pleasure in pains. I do not discard pains. One who has no sense of pleasure does not care for safety and security. I am not the one who has no sense to desire for anything. I am he who also has desire, and my desire is the search of death. I am of that sense which enjoys the pleasure of wounds in search of wounds. I am not the one to go about every shop for gain. I am the one to take a long jump to cross over the world and search for the mine where I find gems of the gnosis of God.

My getting into this masjid is my desire, and meeting death is a sweet for me, just as leaving the cage and flying out is for a caged bird. The cage is in the centre of the garden and the bird is looking at the garden, birds and trees. There are flocks of birds all around the cage, who are reciting the stories of freedom in great pleasure. Because of its confinement within the cage, the bird with beautiful green sceneries outside, has neither hunger nor patience and pleasure. It brings out its head out of every opening of the cage thinking that it may remove the chains from its feet. Imagine what pleasure will be caused to the bird if the door of the cage is opened fulfilling the desires of its heart and soul to fly in the surroundings outside.

But on the contrary, the bird which is full of griefs in the cage sees that there are cats all around the cage. Such a bird will not have the desire to get freedom from the prison of cage in spite of its pains and fears. It will desire that, as against this single cage, there should be hundred cages all around.

chapters.title: Man: Victim of Ignorance
chapters.subtitle: To explain that Galen, the famous Greek physician had love for the world as his great expertise was useful here. He had not learned that science which was useful in the market of the other world, where he would be one among the masses; where the absolute command on that day is Allah’s: Wa alamur yowmainzin lillah (Infitar: 82: 19)

paras: Galen, the famous Greek physician, considered as the founder of the science of medicine, in his love and aspiration of the world said: Even when I am half dead, I am agreeable to see the world even from the back side of the mule. He sees cats all around him in ranks and ranks (to study the world through them), but the bird of his soul has lost hopes of flights. Or he has considered everything other than this material world as non-existent. But he has not seen the turmoil and disturbances hidden in the non-material world.

God’s grace drags out a baby from the womb, but he hesitates and pushes himself toward the other side of the womb. God’s benevolence pulls him towards the exit door, but he holds on tightly to the back of the mother, saying: “if I get out of this city, to my misfortune, I shall not be able to see this place again. Had there been a window to my dirty dwelling of the womb, I would have seen the outside world through it. If not a window, even if it were a narrow eyelet. I would have peeped out to see the world outside the womb”. In this manner the baby is ignorant of this world. So also, was Galen about the world, beyond this material world.

sections.heading: Man’s Ignorance of the Unseen World
paras: The baby does not know that the liquids in the womb have come from things out of the womb. Similarly, the materials made of the four elements (earth, water, air and fire) also receive support from the city of non-space (spiritual world). Whatever grain and water that is found in the cage comes from the gardens and farmlands outside it. The souls of the prophets see these gardens that are out of this world in spite of living in the cage of this material world. Therefore, they are not dependent upon Galen and this world, just like the bright moon in the sky.

If you say that Galen has not said all this, then, I will say that what I said is not about Galen, but about him who has said this, whose heart has not been a friend of spiritual light. The bird of his soul has become like a rat searching for a hole after sighting the approaching cats trying to catch it. That is why his soul has made this world as his country and residence, like the rat which has made its hole. By adopting to art of construction suiting to this “hole”, man has subordinated his wisdom to such limitations. He has learnt other professions that increase his possessions in this “hole”. He has turned his heart away from the ways of exit from this hole and his paths are closed and do not allow him to pass out.

If the spider had the neck of an ostrich, it would not have built its web in high places with its own saliva. Death, like the cat’s paw in the cage of man, causes diseases like fits, epilepsy, dysentery, smallpox, melancholia, mental shock, leprosy etc. This cat is the death and diseases are its paw, which strike at the wings and feathers of the bird of man. He runs about here and there for medicine.

sections.heading: Death as a Judge
paras: But death is like the judge and diseases is its witness. This witness comes as a court officer of the judge to call you to the judge’s court. You seek an adjournment, and if the judge grants it, you are saved in time as otherwise he will say: get going to the next world. Seeking adjournments and medicines are like timely remedies so that you may put patches on the clothes of your body. At last, it comes on a fine day, and no adjournment will be granted, and you are put to shame.

You are jealous of others. Seek pardon from the king before the day of the call of death comes. One who gallops on his horse in darkness keeps his heart away from light. He runs away from the witness of the court which comes as disease, as he knows that the witness is calling him toward the judge of death. He will be caught suddenly and put to disgrace and humility and dragged with all shame toward the judge of death.
Now, leave this affair, and go toward that person who came as a guest in the mosque.

chapters.title: Brave and the Cowards
chapters.subtitle: Condemnation of the guest for his determination to sleep in the mosque

paras: People told him not to hurry so that his life and clothes are not pledged to death. Saying: “Look at carefully. Any object appears very easy from a distance, but the way to it is full of difficulties. Many persons have misunderstood things in the beginning and gone atop and hanged themselves in great hopes but sought for help after getting into difficulties. Good and bad aspects of things can be thought of better before the occurrence of an incident. An inexperienced fellow gets into anxieties upon getting caught in difficulties. When he enters into the battlefield, his job becomes very difficult to do.

sections.heading: Actual and Verbal Boldness
paras: Do not put your steps forward, if you are not brave like a lion, as death is dangerous like the wolf and your life is weak like a goat. But if you are among the ABDALS (saintly people who have converted human vices into virtues) and your goat is converted into a lion, you may remain contented. Death will bow down its head. Who is an ABDAL? He is one who gets changed. With the support of God, his wine gets changed to vinegar. But you are semi-conscious. You suspect yourself to be lion. Be warned! Do not go forward. God has said about the misguided hypocrites. Baasuhum bainahum shadidun, tahsibuhum jamiuin wa qulubuhum shattaa: their fighting among themselves is very great. You think them as a whole, whereas their hearts are diverse. (Hashr: 59: 14).

They are very bold among themselves. But in the battlefield, they are like homely women. The general of the armies of the unseen, the noble Prophet, has said: “Bravery has no worth before the actual battle”. While talking of Jihad well before it, they beat the chest in pride and boast of boldness, and when the actual battle starts, instead of showing their courage, they lay down like lather. At the time of discussions of battle, their sword is very long, but when it comes to hitting outright in the battle front; or take a step backward to hit with greater force their sword becomes short and soft like onion. In their thoughts, they are bloated warriors, but with a prick of needle, their goatskin shrinks.

sections.heading: Claim and Evidence of God’s Love
paras: Similarly, I feel amazed at the fellow who thinks of cleansing his heart, but hesitates to struggle and puts efforts for it (Mujahida). Making a claim of the love of God is a pleading; and undergoing pains for it is the evidence. If you do not have an evidence, your pleading gets lost. Do not be sorry, if the judge of your claim demands evidence for your claim, because without undergoing sufferings nothing can be achieved, as is the belief that treasures are watched and protected by snakes, and these can be taken over only by befriending the snakes. It should be clear to you that the sufferings you cause are not upon you but upon your own vicious qualities.

sections.heading: Beatings for a Good Purpose
paras: In the world of senses, its example is like the beatings that one makes upon a blanket. The beating is not on the blanket but upon the dust accumulated in it. Beatings remove the dust. If someone lashes at a horse, it is not on the horse but on the slackness developed in it. This lashing removes slackness making the horse smart and fast. similarly sugar juice is imprisoned in a pot so as to make it into wine.

A teacher was beating his pupil, which was actually sugar but appearing like troublesome poison. The boy was crying in pain. A person felt pity and took him in his lap and told the teacher: “Why do you beat him like this. Are you not afraid of the wrath of God”? The teacher said: “When have I beaten him? I was beating the Satan that has penetrated into him. If your mother curses you, saying: May God cause your death; she means the death of your bad habits and mischiefs.

sections.heading: Beware of the Cowardly
paras: Such of the people who ran away from disciplining, caused disgrace to humans and humanity. Hypocrites prevented some people from going to the battle and made them into cowards and eunuchs. Do not go after the blabberings of the boasters and braggers and do not go with them for battle. God has said about them: wa louw kharaju fiikum maa zaadukum illa khabaala: if they had come out with you, they would not have added to your strength but only (made for) disorder: (Tauba: 9: 47). Do not ever be in their company but turn to others for learning. Because if they accompany you, other bold fighters will become useless like grass. They will join you, but run away from you, causing disorder in the ranks and discouragement to bold fighters. An army of a few bold soldiers is better than a large one with hypocrites.

sections.heading: Mix Up of Bold and Cowards Is Bad
paras: A few selected sweet, tasty almonds are better than those mixed up with bitter ones. Both the sweet and bitter are the same to look at, and their quality is due to their internal content. A rejecter has a fearful heart, because he lives in suspicions. He has no faith in the other world. He passes on the way without knowing the destination. A man with a blind heart, puts his steps with fears. A traveller cannot move boldly when he does not know the road. He takes slow, heartless steps in fear. If someone tells that this in not the way, he stops there itself out of fear. But one who is certain never cares for any kind of obstructions and objections.

Therefore, do not go forward with these cowardly camel-hearted fellows, as they will go back in times of risk and fear. They will run away and leave you alone. They are great only in boasting like the magicians of Babylonia. Be warned! Do not expect boldness from the effeminate showy fellows in the battlefield and do not expect the peacocks to search for preys. Your showy ostentatious nature puts insinuations in your heart and cheats you, to prevent you from going up to high levels.

chapters.title: Ways of Satan’s Insinuations
chapters.subtitle: Satan’s inducement to the Quraish in the form of Suraaqa Najdi to fight against the Prophet at the time of the battle of Badr, promising to support them with his tribe, but running away at the start of the battle Satan beats a retreat

paras: (This betrayal of the hypocrites) is like the insinuations that Satan blew in the hearts of tribe of Quraish at Makka, to collect an army so that they might defeat Prophet Muhammad and remove the roots of his religion from earth. When Satan became one among the hundred and first soldier, he blew the magic spell: I am your protector: inni jaarunlakum (Anfal: 8: 48). The details of the promise, deal and betrayal as stated in the Quran’s words are: And when Satan joined their deeds favourable to him and said: No one of mankind can conquer you this day, for I am your protector. But when the armies came in sight of one another, he took to flight, saying: “Lo! I am guiltless of you. Lo! I fear Allah. And Allah is severe in punishment.” (Anfal: 8: 48).

When the soldiers gathered, he told them: “I shall bring my family to help you in the battlefield. I shall support you as a friend so as to defeat the soldiers of the enemy.” When the Quraish assembled believing his words, and both the armies came face to face, Satan saw an army of angels coming toward the ranks of the mumins; that army of hosts you could not see: junudan lam tarowha (Ahzaab: 33: 9), his life frightened, as though it was in a furnace. He started dragging his feet backward fearing: “I am seeing a strange army. I am afraid of God. I am not receiving any help from Him. Run away. I am seeing what you do not see”.

Haaris bin Hasham, who had struck the deal with Satan said to him! “O the one resembling Suraqa (one of the Makkan leaders), why did you not say so yesterday”. Satan replied: “I am seeing a great hardship”. Haris said: “You are seeing the beggars from among the Arabs, and nothing else, you are a funny fellow. Yesterday was a time for bragging, but now it is a time of battle. Yesterday, you were telling that you assure us that we shall be dominant at every step and we shall be victorious. O accursed fellow, you were the commander of the army yesterday; and now you act as a coward, worthless and lowly fellow. You said so much that we were trapped by your words. You went into the furnace and we became its fuel.”

When Haris said this to him, Satan was wild, out of anger and withdrew his hand from Haris’s hand, as his words had caused him much pain. He gave a blow on his chest and ran away. With this treachery, those fellows got their blood spilled. After destroying their world, he said: “I am not concerned with you”. he got terrorised and beat his own chest, felled Haris and ran away.

sections.heading: Meaning of Khannas
paras: Nafs (inner mischief) and Satan were one and the same. They showed themselves with different faces. Mischief of Nafs is that of the Satan. They were one, just as angel and wisdom were one and the same. Due to a design of God, they have become different. You have such an enemy within yourself, which is an obstacle to wisdom and enemy of life(soul) and religion. It makes a surprise attack on you like a lizard, runs away and gets back into its hole. It has made many holes in the heart of man and shows its head from all these holes.

sections.heading: Treacheriest Porcupine
paras: As Satan’s work is to cheat man and then hide himself in these holes, he is called as Khannas in the Quran. Its penetrating into the hole is also like that of the porcupine like its head’s coming out and getting inside. This devil is called by God as Khannas as he is like the head of the porcupine. Porcupine has sharp spines on its body within which it hides its head when there is fear of being preyed upon. And when occasion arises, it brings out its head and treacherously attacks the enemy with such skill that even snakes get killed by it.

sections.heading: Greatest Misguidance: Nafs
paras: If your Nafs were not to misguide you from inside, there would be no scope of dacoity from outside. This pressing misguidance is your worldly desire, which makes your heart a prisoner of greed, excessiveness and hardships. Because of this hidden misguidance, you become a thief and get spoiled, so much so, the police get an opportunity to trouble you. You may take this advice from the Hadith(s): “Your greatest enemy is between your two arms.” Do not ever take the decorative advice of this enemy, and run away from it, is like showing its grandeur in quarrels and fights.

Nafs has made perpetual torture as a matter of comfort for you out of enmity and love for this world. It can project death as an easy matter for you. With its magic it can make it appear easy by a hundred times. Magic projects a mountain as a scrap and then a scrap as a mountain. Mischiefs are projected as virtues and through wrong speculations and virtues as vices. In a moment it can make a donkey of a man and a man of a donkey. The job of the magic is only to blow a breath and turn realities into falsities.

sections.heading: Good and Bad Magic
